modules.name: Site wind climate and reference wind statistics
modules.effort: M-L: 8-10 person-days (ECCC and ISD parsing with ragged rows and calm rules, StationSplice, UTC/LST handling, per-sector exposure transfer, two time bases, ReferenceSpec, wind rose, stability tags, data-quality badge, regression fixtures)
modules.design_question: Which wind directions and speeds, by season and hour of use, drive pedestrian wind here on a stated reference, and are the record, its splice and the exposure correction adequate?
inputs: Layer 0 georeference and true-north offset (VTC site-plan north arrow is rotated relative to the street grid)

Hourly station record (speed, direction, temperature, humidity), 30 years or more, by one of two routes: (A) ECCC hourly CSV for Vancouver Int'l A (climate ID 1108447, station 889, hourly 1953-2013) spliced to Vancouver Intl A (1108395, station 51442, hourly 2013-2026); (B) NOAA ISD 718920-99999 (one id throughout). ECCC stamps are LST (UTC-8), ISD stamps are UTC
StationSplice record: both climate IDs, splice hour, overlap statistics (ECCC overlap 11 Jun 06:00 to 13 Jun 10:00 LST 2013, 51 h), anemometer or exposure change notes from ECCC metadata

EPW/TMYx file (typical-year time base; header time zone -8.0, daylight saving No; header source 'NCEI ISD/ERA5') for solar and for the TMYx WindClimate (feeds M06); the Vancouver.Harbour.CS TMYx is refused as a wind source
Station metadata: anemometer height, observation sampling period (1, 2 or 10 min), terrain roughness at the station
Per-sector upwind roughness table: z0, displacement height and fetch length for each 22.5 degree sector (water versus city), drawn from a map and logged; gradient height (Toronto example 600 m)

Optional QA and proxy inputs: gust from ECCC daily Spd of Max Gust or the ISD OC1 group (sparse, QA only; the hourly CSV has no gust column); sky cover from ISD GF1 or EPW total sky cover (the hourly CSV has no cloud column)
outputs: WindClimate[concurrent-30y] and WindClimate[TMYx]: hourly series (speed, direction, season tag, comfort-hour flag with the window stated in LST, stability tag, concurrent temperature and humidity), stored in UTC with an LST field, each with a record id (station ids, years, splice) and its own ReferenceSpec

ReferenceSpec (one per WindClimate): z_ref (default 120 m), per-sector z0 table, displacement and gradient height, profile law, sampling period, direction reference (true north), time zone, transfer model and version
WindRoseTable: 16 sectors x speed bins x season, plus a separate calm class (speed 0, any direction field) and a variable-direction class
NorthOffset (degrees)
StationSplice (ids, splice hour, continuity statistics, ISD comparison)
DataQualityBadge (record length, completeness, splice status, exposure mismatch, calm share, sampling period and time zone declared, sky-cover coverage)

parameters.name: Hourly wind record length
parameters.relationship: Longer record (30 years minimum in Toronto and Hamilton; RWDI Cambridge used 20) -> steadier frequencies of rare events such as the 0.1% safety gust (about 9 h/yr) -> more reliable pass/fail. Sensitivity not quantified.

parameters.name: Station record splice
parameters.relationship: A 30-year window ending after June 2013 spans two ECCC climate IDs (1108447, 1108395). A step at the splice would shift exceedances for the whole record, so the overlap is tested and logged; NOAA ISD keeps one id throughout.

parameters.name: Comfort hours and season split
parameters.relationship: Comfort uses 06:00-23:00 winds in Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI, safety 24 h; City of London states no hours window and reports worst season plus June-August. Annual averages hide storm-season exceedances.

parameters.name: Time zone of records and comfort window
parameters.relationship: ECCC stamps Local Standard Time (UTC-8), ISD stamps UTC, the TMYx header gives -8.0 and no daylight saving. Joining unconverted stamps pairs wrong hours; reading 06:00-23:00 as clock time shifts the window one hour while daylight saving applies.

parameters.name: Per-sector upwind roughness (fetch)
parameters.relationship: Some sectors cross Burrard Inlet, English Bay or False Creek, others dense city (Eddy3D: terrain the wind crosses upwind). One z0 biases sectors in opposite directions and mis-sets the flow reaching 244-305 m tower height.

parameters.name: Transfer model and gradient height
parameters.relationship: Toronto scales terrain-corrected data to gradient height (600 m example); City of London uses ESDU 01008 with Harris-Deaves profiles and a 120 m reference. An uncapped log law keeps rising above gradient height and overstates tower-top speed.

parameters.name: Reference height (ReferenceSpec)
parameters.relationship: City of London scale factors run from 0.96 (100 m) to 1.48 (600 m) for one climate, normalised at 120 m. A reference mismatch with the VAF scales every probe speed and shifts comfort classes; default 120 m, at least 100 m.

parameters.name: Observation sampling period (metadata only)
parameters.relationship: ECCC hourly speed is one sampled 1-, 2- or 10-minute mean (2-minute at aviation stations since the late 1980s): no bias in the mean, extra scatter that slightly overstates rare high-speed exceedances (reasoned, size unquantified). No factor is applied; the period is logged.

parameters.name: True-north offset of the site plan
parameters.relationship: ECCC directions are true north, so only the site-plan rotation needs correcting. A wrong offset assigns wind to the wrong facade by the same angle, shifting where downwash and corner flows are predicted.

parameters.name: Time-base concurrency
parameters.relationship: Temperature, humidity and wind from one record keep cold-and-windy hours together for M06; mixing a typical-year file with a 30-year wind record scrambles them, so M01 emits one WindClimate per time base. Logical rule, no source.

parameters.name: Calms and atmospheric stability
parameters.relationship: The ECCC hourly CSV marks a calm as speed 0 with an empty direction (never direction 0); ISD uses type C with direction 999. Calms stay in every denominator. Stable hours (Arctic outflow, clear nights) and sea breezes break neutral transfer, so their share is reported separately.

metrics.name: Hourly record length
metrics.good: >= 30 years of hourly data, with a documented StationSplice if the window ends after June 2013 (for example 1996-2025)
metrics.bad: < 30 years, or two climate IDs merged without a splice record
metrics.method: Count years with adequate hourly coverage across the splice (the completeness threshold is user-set)
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR 6.4.4 and Hamilton 2026 both specify at least 30 years of hourly data; RWDI Cambridge used 1995-2015, so 30 years is a municipal rule, not universal. Populated hours in two sample years: YVR 2000 8,780 of 8,784; YVR 2024 8,766 of 8,784

metrics.name: Station splice continuity
metrics.good: StationSplice stores both climate IDs, the splice hour, overlap statistics and any anemometer or exposure change note; the ISD record 718920-99999 is compared as a second source
metrics.bad: Two IDs joined silently, a break in speed or direction statistics unreported, or the 2013 overlap unchecked
metrics.method: Compare overlap hours (ECCC 11 Jun 06:00 to 13 Jun 10:00 LST 2013: 51 h, mean difference +0.41 km/h new minus old, maximum 4 km/h, directions equal in 35 h and one 10 degree code apart in 16 h); compare ISD with each side (June 2013 mean absolute difference 0.34 and 0.6 km/h, mean near 0)
metrics.basis: IDs and hourly year ranges from the ECCC station inventory (30 Sep 2026); overlap statistics computed from the hourly CSVs in r3. No sourced tolerance exists, so pass tolerances are user-set; anemometer changes are not documented in the sources opened

metrics.name: Season and hour convention declared
metrics.good: Declared set: Toronto four seasons; Hamilton and RWDI two (May-Oct, Nov-Apr); City of London worst season plus Jun-Aug; comfort 06:00-23:00 for Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI; City Lawson 24 h (no hours window stated); safety 24 h
metrics.bad: Annual-only statistics, all-hours comfort for a 06:00-23:00 family, or 06:00-23:00 imposed on the City Lawson set
metrics.method: Check run configuration against the selected CriteriaSet
metrics.basis: Toronto 5.3 and 6.4.4; Hamilton technical requirement 3; RWDI Cambridge report; City of London results section (seasons, no hours window)

metrics.name: Time-zone alignment
metrics.good: Every series stored in UTC with an LST field; the comfort window is defined in LST (default 06:00-23:00 LST, editable, logged in the CriteriaSet); joins refuse series with different time-zone metadata
metrics.bad: Series joined on local timestamps from different sources, or the window left as an unstated local time
metrics.method: Read the zone from the ECCC header (LST), ISD (UTC) and EPW header (-8.0, daylight saving No); test with overlap hours
metrics.basis: ECCC column header reads Date/Time (LST); ISD 08:00 UTC on 1 Jan 2025 matches ECCC 00:00 LST (80 degrees, 5 kt versus 10 km/h) and the next three hours match in direction; YVR TMYx header gives -8.0 and daylight saving No, and June GHI peaks at hours 12-13 (658 and 650 W/m2), consistent with standard time. Toronto and Hamilton state 06:00-23:00 with no time zone, so LST is a team choice

metrics.name: ReferenceSpec completeness
metrics.good: z_ref (default 120 m, at least 100 m), per-sector z0 and fetch, displacement and gradient height, profile law, sampling period, time zone and direction reference declared; transfer model and version logged
metrics.bad: Any field missing, a single z0 for all sectors, or station speed used as site speed
metrics.method: Schema check on each WindClimate before release to M03-M06
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.4 requires terrain-corrected data scaled to gradient height; City of London wants a stated reference ideally above 100 m, a climate scaled to 120 m and ESDU 01008 corrections. The 120 m default is London's convention applied to Vancouver

metrics.name: Per-sector exposure table
metrics.good: Roughness, displacement and fetch length per 22.5 degree sector from a map, water sectors separated from city sectors, transfer model named
metrics.bad: One z0 for all sectors
metrics.method: Draw upwind fetch polygons per sector on the site map; assign a Revised Davenport class (0.0002-2 m range in the Eddy3D docs) and log it; run the named transfer per sector
metrics.basis: Eddy3D defines terrain as what the wind crosses upwind; City of London names ESDU 01008. The per-sector rule is a design choice and no Vancouver roughness values were found

metrics.name: Sampling period declared, no mean-level conversion
metrics.good: Sampling period (1, 2 or 10 min) logged from metadata; sampled speeds used as hourly-mean estimates; no multiplicative conversion
metrics.bad: A gust-factor or averaging-time factor applied to station means, or station gust used for pedestrian statistics
metrics.method: Read the period from station metadata (aviation stations: 2 min since the late 1980s, 1 min before); log only
metrics.basis: ECCC glossary and technical documentation define one sampled mean ending at the observation; Toronto and Hamilton ask for hourly data with no conversion; the earlier 'inflated exceedances' claim is corrected. Sampling scatter slightly overstates rare high-speed exceedances (conservative; reasoned, size unquantified)

metrics.name: Station representativeness
metrics.good: Station exposure and airshed comparable to the downtown site, with documented correction; a downtown cross-check shown only if an anemometer record of at least 10 years is verified
metrics.bad: Uncorrected airport data used as site wind, or Vancouver Harbour CS (or its TMYx) cited as a downtown wind cross-check
metrics.method: Compare station and site roughness and distance (YVR to Harbour CS 13.0 km); log the correction model; refuse the Harbour CS TMYx as a wind file
metrics.basis: Harbour CS (station 888) hourly CSVs hold wind from 20 Jan 1976 to at least 31 Mar 1988 and none in sampled months from Apr 1988 to Jan 2026; VANCOUVER HARBOUR (55438) files are timestamp-only; ISD Harbour CS WND is missing in Jan 2015. Harbour CS TMYx 2011-2025: mean 1.0 m/s, 50.3% zero-speed hours, maximum 6.6 m/s, against YVR TMYx 3.85 m/s, 3.6%, 19.0 m/s. The earlier claim of a usable Harbour CS wind cross-check is corrected

metrics.name: Concurrent time base per WindClimate
metrics.good: One WindClimate per time base (concurrent-30y, TMYx), each with its record id and ReferenceSpec; temperature, humidity and wind from the same record; exposure correction applied to both
metrics.bad: Typical-year temperature with a 30-year wind record, uncorrected EPW airport wind, or a 30-year record whose spliced IDs are not documented
metrics.method: Tag each series with record id and years; refuse to merge series across time bases; allow a merge of two station IDs only through a documented StationSplice; apply the per-sector transfer to the TMYx wind too
metrics.basis: Design rule for M04 and M06. r3 correction: the no-merge rule had barred any 30-year window ending after 2013 because the YVR record changed climate ID; it now applies between time bases, not inside a documented splice. TMYx header reads 'NCEI ISD/ERA5', so the origin of each hour is unverified

metrics.name: Calm hours handled
metrics.good: Calm = speed 0 whatever the direction field holds (empty in the ECCC CSV, 999 with type C in ISD, any value in the TMYx); own class, left out of the 16 sector bins, kept in every exceedance denominator; empty or 999 direction with speed above 0 goes to a variable class; calm share on the badge
metrics.bad: Calms detected by 'direction 0' (never fires on the ECCC CSV), dropped as missing (exceedance E becomes E/(1 - calm share)), or binned into the north sector
metrics.method: speed = 0 -> calm; tolerate timestamp-only rows. Regression fixtures with expected counts: station 889 Jan 2000 (744 rows, 58 calm) and Jul 2010 (37); station 51442 Jan 2025 (744 rows, 3 timestamp-only, 90 calm of 741) and Jul 2020 (22)
metrics.basis: ECCC glossary and technical documentation describe direction 0/00 as calm, but the hourly CSV leaves direction empty on every speed-0 hour (full-year counts: 2000 542 of 8,780 populated hours, 6.2%; 2024 272 of 8,766, 3.1%; none with direction 0). Dropping calms inflates exceedance: a true 17.6% reads 20.0% at a 12.1% calm share (Jan 2025), 18.8% at 6.2%, 19.4% at 3.1%

metrics.name: Stability tag
metrics.good: Hours tagged with an editable proxy: night flag from computed solar elevation, wind-speed class, season, and sky cover only where a source has it (ISD GF1, EPW total sky cover); outflow-hour share reported beside neutral statistics; sky-cover coverage on the badge
metrics.bad: Neutral transfer applied silently to Arctic-outflow or clear-night hours, or a cloud column assumed in the ECCC hourly CSV
metrics.method: Proxy rule logged with the run; thresholds are user-editable; log which sky source was used
metrics.basis: No sourced proxy thresholds; Arctic outflow 1-3 times per winter (Climate of Vancouver). ECCC hourly Weather text names a sky state in 74% (Jan 2000), 99% (Jul 2010), 31% (Jul 2020), 29% (Jan 2025) of hours; ISD GF1 total coverage is valid in 608/608 hourly records (Jan 1985), 132/744 (Jan 2015), 331/732 (Jan 2025); EPW total sky cover is complete (8,760 of 8,760 in the YVR TMYx)

modules.method: 1) Read the hourly record: ECCC CSV (LST; timestamp-only rows tolerated) spliced across climate IDs 1108447 and 1108395 with an overlap test, or ISD 718920-99999 (UTC); store UTC plus an LST field. 2) Direction is true north, rotated by the Layer 0 offset; calm = speed 0 whatever the direction field holds, kept in the denominator; empty or 999 direction with speed above 0 goes to a variable class; spread each 10 degree code over 22.5 degree sectors proportionally (team choice). 3) Log the sampling period; no mean-level conversion. 4) Build the per-sector table and transfer each sector to the reference height (default 120 m) with a named model (Deaves-Harris/ESDU 01008, or a log law capped at gradient height); write the ReferenceSpec. 5) Tag stability and season; bin sectors, speed classes and seasons for comfort hours (window in LST) and 24 h safety hours. 6) Emit one WindClimate per time base with concurrent temperature and humidity and a badge. 7) Rank seasons from the data.
visualization: Polar wind rose per season (16 sectors, stacked speed bins in km/h) with the calm share in the centre, one panel per season, true-north arrow and rotated street-grid axis overlaid

Polar bar chart of z0 per sector (log scale) over a map thumbnail, water sectors blue and city sectors grey, beside a bar chart of hours per sector above 20 km/h at z_ref per season and a season-ranking table computed from the data

Data-quality badge (green/amber/red) with a ReferenceSpec card (z_ref, per-sector z0, sampling period, time zone, transfer model, time base) linking to the Toronto and City of London clauses, plus a splice panel: scatter of overlap-hour speeds (old versus new climate ID) with a 1:1 line and the mean difference printed

libraries.role: Named transfer model for roughness changes and the boundary-layer profile; ESDU is a paid document and was not opened, so implement a capped log law first and add Deaves-Harris as an option

modules.limits: TMY/EPW files are constructed typical years (header 'NCEI ISD/ERA5'), so rare storms are under-represented and the origin of each hour is unverified. Airport anemometers differ from downtown exposure and no downtown wind record is verified. ECCC speeds are single 1-10 minute samples in integer km/h with 10 degree direction codes. Per-sector roughness values are team estimates; ESDU 01008 was not opened. Stability is tagged, not modelled. Pedestrian statistics are not P10's 1-in-50-year design wind. The climate is stationary.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the ECCC splice or the ISD record, accepting the splice overlap, drawing the per-sector fetch map, choosing the transfer model, deciding whether site data or a consultant study is needed, and interpreting local flows such as winter outflow, sea breezes and storm winds.

modules.name: Wind-study requirement and criteria selector
modules.effort: S-M: 5-6 person-days (rule tables, five versioned CriteriaSets, inclusion rules, precedent table, analog-criteria label and export check, clause-linked report)
modules.design_question: Will this massing probably need a formal pedestrian wind study in Vancouver, and which comfort and safety criteria set, with its own safety limit, should the tool apply and cite?
inputs: Layer 0: maximum tower height, count of buildings at or above 20 m, site area
Context building heights from the SITE module, including approved and future towers named in the VTC brief
Program tags: entrances, seating, transit plaza, amenity terraces, cycle routes
User choice of criteria family and trigger preset
VancouverPrecedentTable: manual entries from 2-3 downtown rezoning wind reports (criteria family, station, seasons, hours, conditions), empty until a named team member downloads them
outputs: StudyTriggerReport (per analog jurisdiction: Toronto 2022, Hamilton 2026, City of London 2019; clause links and document status)

CriteriaSet: versioned typed JSON (family and version, classes, speeds and units, exceedance basis, averaging as mean or GEM, comfort hours and their time zone, seasons, zone-to-class map, mandatory safety criterion or explicit none, source id, status) consumed by M04 and M06
ScenarioChecklist (existing / proposed / proposed plus approved towers / demolished-site case if the existing building is over 40 m / mitigation / phasing)
ContextSpec: minimum context radius, inclusion rules and cumulative tower list for M03 and M05
PrecedentCheck: default CriteriaSet compared with the PrecedentTable once filled

AnalogCriteriaLabel: fixed text (family and version, 'team assumption', 'no City of Vancouver numeric criteria found', precedent count) that M04, M07, M08 and the PRES board export print on every comfort or safety map, chip and table until the PrecedentTable holds at least 2 reports

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: Taller tower -> higher trigger level and a tunnel requirement: Toronto Area 1 over 100 m is High, Hamilton 44 m or more, City of London above 100 m needs tunnel and CFD at detailed design. VTC towers of 244-305 m exceed every analog threshold found.

parameters.name: Height relative to surrounding buildings
parameters.relationship: Hamilton requires a tunnel study when a building of 20 m or more exceeds twice its surroundings; City of London steps up to CFD and tunnel at up to 4 times average surrounding height. Taller relative to context -> stricter study.

parameters.name: Number of buildings of 20 m or more
parameters.relationship: Two or more tall buildings move Toronto projects up one trigger level and trigger a tunnel study in Hamilton; multi-tower schemes therefore face stricter study types.

parameters.name: Criteria family and exceedance basis
parameters.relationship: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI limit GEM at 20% exceedance; City Lawson limits mean and GEM at 5%. Safety differs too: 90 km/h at 0.1% against 15 m/s at 0.022%. One family per run, never mixed.

parameters.name: Modelled context radius and cumulative scenario
parameters.relationship: Toronto asks about 350 m, Hamilton and City of London 400 m, plus influential taller buildings beyond. Larger radius and inclusion of approved towers -> truer approach flow and sheltering; the VTC brief names approved towers, so the cumulative case is required.

parameters.name: Context inclusion rules
parameters.relationship: City of London includes consented or future buildings immediately around the site at any height, and those taller than the surrounding average within 300 m, plus a demolished-site case if the existing building exceeds 40 m. Omitting them misstates sheltering.

parameters.name: Vegetation and small features in the baseline
parameters.relationship: Toronto does not consider landscaping unless agreed with the City; City of London ignores landscape under 8 m and models features projecting over 0.5 m near pedestrians. Taking planting credit in baseline runs would understate wind.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion
parameters.relationship: Policy criterion says a higher building should not contribute to adverse microclimate effects; it has no number, so the team must adopt numeric criteria and state why. Wording seen only in search snippets of the 2011/2018 versions.

metrics.name: Toronto-analog trigger level (downtown Area 1)
metrics.good: Low: over 20 m and under 60 m (CFD Phase 1 and 2 only)
metrics.bad: High: over 100 m (CFD Phase 1 plus wind-tunnel study at rezoning)
metrics.method: Compare tower height and context with Toronto Table 1 and the 3.b shift rules
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR Tables 1 and 2, re-read in r1

metrics.name: Hamilton-analog trigger
metrics.good: Under 20 m: no study
metrics.bad: 44 m or more, or 20 m+ and over 2x surroundings, or 2+ buildings of 20 m+: quantitative wind-tunnel study
metrics.method: Evaluate Hamilton rules 1-3 on Layer 0
metrics.basis: Hamilton guidelines, last updated 20 Feb 2026; adoption status unconfirmed (file name says 'ph1proposed')

metrics.name: City of London-analog trigger
metrics.good: Similar to or lower than surroundings and up to 25 m: no study unless sensitive uses
metrics.bad: Above 100 m: tunnel or CFD for massing, then tunnel and CFD by independent consultants at detailed design
metrics.method: Compare height and average surrounding height with the City of London approach table
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 table of recommended approach by building height

metrics.name: Vancouver Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion
metrics.good: No adverse microclimate effects (qualitative)
metrics.bad: Adverse microclimate effects
metrics.method: Present as qualitative pass/flag linked to the chosen numeric criteria in M04
metrics.basis: 2011/2018 policy wording seen only in search snippets; the 1997 PDF named in the brief was not opened (HTTP 403 in r1, r2 and again r3)

metrics.name: Default criteria set for Vancouver runs
metrics.good: Toronto 2022 three-class set (10/15/20 km/h GEM at 80%), editable; Hamilton 2026 is equal or stricter at every shared class
metrics.bad: Unstated or mixed criteria
metrics.method: Preset selection stored with the run and shown in every result with the AnalogCriteriaLabel
metrics.basis: No Vancouver numeric criteria found. Toronto chosen as the downtown tall-building analog with an explicit High tier, a verified zone-to-class table and three classes. Attempts to obtain downtown Vancouver rezoning wind reports failed in r1-r3 (all City of Vancouver hosts returned 403), so the default stays a team assumption until the PrecedentTable is filled by hand

metrics.name: Analog-criteria label on every output
metrics.good: Label printed on every ComfortMap, SafetyFlags table, chip and board export while the PrecedentTable holds fewer than 2 reports; wording: 'Criteria: [family, version] analog (team assumption). No City of Vancouver numeric criteria found. Precedent reports: n'
metrics.bad: Any comfort or safety output, image or PRES board without the label, so Ontario or UK classes read as Vancouver compliance
metrics.method: Export validator refuses a board or image export that contains a comfort or safety layer without the label string; label text changes only when the table reaches 2 reports
metrics.basis: Design rule from the r3 critique; PrecedentTable has 0 reports and no City of Vancouver numeric criteria were found. The 2-report threshold is a team choice

metrics.name: Vancouver precedent evidence
metrics.good: At least two downtown Vancouver rezoning wind reports tabulated (criteria family, station, seasons, hours, mitigation conditions) and the default CriteriaSet justified from them
metrics.bad: None obtained: default remains an Ontario-analog team assumption
metrics.method: A named team member downloads reports by hand before 13 Nov (Shape Your City or rezoning applications) and fills the PrecedentTable; M02 compares family, station and hours with the default
metrics.basis: Automated fetches of vancouver.ca, rezoning.vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, syc.vancouver.ca and council.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 in r1, r2 and on 21 Oct 2026 (curl and WebFetch); the Bay Parkade FAQ names no wind study; evidence is missing, not negative

metrics.name: CriteriaSet integrity
metrics.good: Each set carries its own classes, exceedance basis, averaging, comfort hours and safety criterion (Toronto 10/15/20 km/h, 06:00-23:00; Hamilton 10/14/17/20; RWDI 6/8/10/12 mph; City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s, 24 h)
metrics.bad: A merged 'RWDI/Toronto' set, Lawson speeds at 20%, 06:00-23:00 imposed on City Lawson, or a set with no safety criterion
metrics.method: Schema validation of each CriteriaSet at load and at run
metrics.basis: Earlier spec merged Toronto's three classes with the four classes of RWDI and Hamilton; corrected after round 1. In r2 the City Lawson comfort hours changed from 06:00-23:00 to 24 h because the guideline states no hours window

metrics.name: Context radius, inclusion rules and scenario set
metrics.good: Radius at least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond; consented or future buildings immediately around the site at any height and those taller than the surrounding average within 300 m; scenarios existing, proposed, proposed plus approved and future towers, demolished-site if existing building over 40 m, mitigation, phasing
metrics.bad: 350 m radius, no cumulative scenario, or omitted inclusion rules
metrics.method: Check ContextSpec against the run; list towers added beyond the radius
metrics.basis: 350 m (Toronto) and 400 m (Hamilton, City of London) are minima with taller buildings beyond to be included; 300 m, immediate-building and 40 m rules are City of London; the 2H term is a team assumption

modules.method: Read maximum tower height, count of buildings of 20 m or more, site area and context heights from Layer 0 and the SITE module. Evaluate each analog rule set (Toronto Table 1 with +1 level shifts, Hamilton rules 1-3, City of London height bands, Barrie 6-storey trigger) and output a level per jurisdiction with clause link and document status. Load the chosen CriteriaSet (classes, speeds, exceedance, averaging, hours and zone, seasons, zone map, safety criterion, source id, status); a set with no safety criterion blocks safety output. Custom edits become team assumptions; wrong claims stay visible as FALSE ASSUMPTION. Emit ContextSpec (radius at least max(400 m, about 2H), City of London inclusion rules, vegetation excluded), the scenario checklist (16 CFD or 36 tunnel directions) and the AnalogCriteriaLabel; compare the default with the PrecedentTable once filled.
visualization: Summary card with four chips (Toronto-analog, Hamilton-analog, City of London-analog, Vancouver policy) coloured pass/flag, each linking to the clause and showing document status, plus a precedent chip (empty / 1 report / 2+ reports) and the AnalogCriteriaLabel banner

Grouped bar chart of comfort thresholds in km/h per category for Toronto, Hamilton, RWDI (mph converted) and City Lawson (m/s converted, hatched because the basis is 5% exceedance on mean and GEM), with a side table of each safety criterion and comfort-hour window
Checklist of required evidence items with ticks, including context radius, inclusion rules, cumulative scenario and the hand-downloaded precedent reports

libraries.role: Validate CriteriaSet records (licence not re-verified)

modules.limits: No City of Vancouver numeric wind criteria or mandatory trigger could be found; every City of Vancouver host returned HTTP 403 in r1-r3, so absence is not proven. Presets are Ontario, RWDI and City of London practice, not Vancouver law, which is why every output carries the analog label. The brief is an academic exercise and its jury may reward justified breaches.
modules.human_judgment: Which criteria family to adopt; one named team member downloading 2-3 downtown rezoning wind reports by hand before 13 Nov and filling the PrecedentTable; how to argue any breach to the jury; confirming with the City Rezoning Centre what a real application would need.

modules.name: Early massing wind-risk screening
modules.effort: M: 7-10 person-days (geometry rules, 3D flag overlay, source-linked reasons)
modules.design_question: Which massing moves (tower height, podium, step-backs, corners, tower gaps, through-block openings) are likely to create downwash, corner acceleration or channelling in the public realm?
inputs: Layer 0 footprints, heights, canopy objects and program tags (vegetation excluded from the baseline)
Context building heights within the ContextSpec radius from M02 (default max(400 m, about 2H))
WindClimate from M01 (prevailing and strong-wind sectors)
Zone tags: entrances, sidewalks, plazas, transit plaza, mid-block connections, cycle routes
outputs: WindRiskField: per-rule Low/Medium/High flags per facade segment, corner and public-space zone, with reason codes and clause links
RankedActions list (largest-scale changes first)
DirectionalExposure table (windward width and exposure height by sector)
PriorityProbes: probe points to seed M04 and M05
CanopyCoverageTable per frontage (to M06)
WindRiskIndex (0-100): computed but hidden until a CalibrationLog exists

parameters.name: Exposure height above upwind context
parameters.relationship: Tower height above the tallest upwind context (sector-weighted) -> more stream intercepted and pushed down onto the base (downwash); short buildings rarely cause adverse impacts. Regulatory ratio triggers such as Hamilton's 2x sit in M02.

parameters.name: Windward facade width
parameters.relationship: Wider windward face -> larger intercepted flow and stronger downwash; Hamilton states tall, wide facades are generally undesirable.

parameters.name: Podium and tower offset from podium edge
parameters.relationship: Podium with a set-back tower deflects downflow before it reaches the street, lowering pedestrian-level speed; Toronto lists tower offset change as a significant wind change. Size of the benefit is not quantified in opened sources.

parameters.name: Lower building directly upwind of the tower
parameters.relationship: A lower upwind building can enlarge downflow on the tower and accelerate wind in the gap and at windward corners, yet shorter buildings upwind of taller ones lower tower exposure. Net effect depends on gap and heights.

parameters.name: Corner geometry
parameters.relationship: Sharp corners -> flow separates and accelerates at pedestrian level; chamfered or rounded corners streamline flow, stepped or re-entrant corners diffuse it, lowering corner speeds.

parameters.name: Gap between buildings aligned with strong-wind sector
parameters.relationship: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI describe channelling in narrow gaps, but idealised steady-RANS canyons gave larger uncomfortable zones at 2x height than at 1x. Effect depends on gap ratio and on whether the gap is a through-passage; no monotonic rule.

parameters.name: Through-block openings, underpasses, colonnades
parameters.relationship: Passages can accelerate flow along mid-block connections, yet passage studies (recalled, not opened) report wind-blocking rather than classic Venturi acceleration; colonnades also act as wind control. Effect depends on orientation and geometry.

parameters.name: Canopies, recessed entrances, covered walkways
parameters.relationship: Deep, wrap-around and corner canopies and recessed entrances intercept downwash and create sheltered waiting zones; effect is local and secondary to massing. Canopy coverage also feeds rain protection in M06.

metrics.name: Exposure height above upwind context
metrics.good: Lower than the baseline scheme in the strongest-wind sectors
metrics.bad: Higher than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Tower top minus the highest upwind roof within the radius, weighted by sector frequency from M01
metrics.basis: Discriminates between options (regulatory height triggers sit in M02 because every VTC scheme is High); no sourced limit

metrics.name: Windward facade width by sector
metrics.good: Narrower than the baseline scheme toward strong-wind sectors
metrics.bad: Wide face toward a strong-wind sector
metrics.method: Projected facade width perpendicular to each 22.5 degree sector
metrics.basis: Direction sourced (Hamilton: tall and wide facades are generally undesirable); no numeric limit

metrics.name: Windward corner treatment
metrics.good: Chamfered, rounded, stepped or re-entrant corners
metrics.bad: Sharp corners on a tall windward volume
metrics.method: Detect corner turning angle and tag treatment
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.7.2 building-form strategies (qualitative)

metrics.name: Tower-podium offset depth
metrics.good: No sourced target; calibrate with M05 runs
metrics.bad: No sourced limit
metrics.method: Measure tower face to podium edge
metrics.basis: Direction of effect sourced, magnitude not; podium and separation literature (Tsang et al. 2012, recalled) not opened

metrics.name: Lower building within one tower height upwind
metrics.good: None within one tower height in a strong-wind sector
metrics.bad: Present within one tower height
metrics.method: Distance from tower to lower upwind buildings along each strong-wind sector
metrics.basis: Mechanism sourced (Toronto, Hamilton); the one-tower-height distance is an editable placeholder

metrics.name: Gap aligned with strong-wind sector
metrics.good: Not aligned (outside one 22.5 degree sector), or a closed-ended gap
metrics.bad: Through-passage aligned within one 22.5 degree sector of a strong-wind direction
metrics.method: Gap axis angle versus sector with strong-wind frequency from M01; tag through-passage or closed gap
metrics.basis: Editable placeholder; mechanism sourced, angle not; gap effect is non-monotonic in an idealised study (S07); the through-passage distinction rests on passage literature not opened

metrics.name: Composite wind-risk index per facade, corner and zone
metrics.good: Shown only after a CalibrationLog (at least about 10 massings with L2 runs) exists, then Low band by editable cut-off
metrics.bad: Shown on boards without calibration (false precision for a jury-facing output)
metrics.method: Weighted sum of rule flags by sector frequency; weights and cut-offs are team assumptions to be recalibrated against CFD; per-rule flags are shown until then
metrics.basis: No sourced scoring scheme and no calibration dataset exist; the count of 10 massings is a team placeholder

modules.method: For each of 16 wind sectors, weighted by seasonal strong-wind frequency from M01: (1) compute each tower's exposure height above the upwind context within the M02 radius and its windward width; (2) detect lower buildings within one tower height upwind (team assumption); (3) find gaps and passages whose axis lies within one sector of the wind, separating through-passages from closed gaps; (4) flag windward corners by turning angle and treatment (sharp, chamfer, round, step); (5) check podium offset and canopy presence at entrance and sidewalk zones. Each rule gives Low/Medium/High with a reason code and clause link. The composite 0-100 index stays hidden until calibrated against L2 runs. Output priority probes for M04/M05 and a canopy-coverage table for M06.
visualization: Plan view of Layer 0 with arrows per strong-wind sector; windward corners as dots and facade segments as lines coloured Low (blue) / Medium (amber) / High (red) by the highest single rule flag
Ground-plane zone polygons shaded by flag count (0-8 rules triggered, legend shown); the composite 0-100 panel stays greyed with the label 'uncalibrated' until a CalibrationLog exists
Radar chart of the eight factors per tower
Reason-code table; each row links to the Toronto/Hamilton/RWDI clause, with a banner stating that this is screening and predicts no speeds

modules.limits: Rule-based screening ranks risk; it does not predict speeds or class compliance. Interaction of several towers, supertall scale (over 244 m), complex context and topography break simple rules, and the gap rule is non-monotonic. Use it to compare options and place CFD probes. Numeric rule cut-offs, including the one-tower-height upwind distance, are unsourced and editable.
modules.human_judgment: Weighing wind against daylight, program, structure and 'City in Nature' placemaking, and deciding how much residual risk the scheme accepts.

modules.name: Pedestrian wind comfort and safety classifier
modules.effort: M: 7-9 person-days in total; core subset (typed VAF import with reference and time-base gates, probe-hour engine, season classes, zone pass/fail, indicative safety, analog label) about 4-5 days; delta, cyclist and low-wind maps follow in v1
modules.design_question: Given directional amplification factors at probes on a stated reference, what comfort class and safety status result per season, and do entrances, sidewalks, plazas, terraces and cycle routes meet their intended use?
inputs: WindClimate[time base] and ReferenceSpec from M01 (concurrent-30y and TMYx), with time-zone metadata

VAFField with its own ReferenceSpec, inflow-profile declaration and homogeneity report: from M05, or a typed CSV import (Eddy3D, wind-tunnel or consultant data) checked against an import template; M05 is optional
ProbeSet with zone tags from Layer 0 (entrance, sidewalk, seating, transit plaza, terrace, cycle route)
CriteriaSet and AnalogCriteriaLabel from M02 (with comfort hours and safety criterion)
Turbulent kinetic energy or turbulence intensity per probe (required for GEM families)
outputs: ReferenceGateReport: pass, or refusal with the mismatched fields (reference, time-base tag, time zone, inflow declaration), or the logged conversion applied
ComfortMap: per probe and season, exceedance fraction (calm hours in the denominator), class, pass/fail against the zone requirement, with the analog label
SafetyFlags (indicative below L3; blocked when the CriteriaSet has no safety criterion)
ZoneComplianceTable and CyclistRouteTable
ProbeWindSeries per time base: hourly mean and GEM series at the probe, with time-base tag, time zone and ReferenceSpec, for M06

parameters.name: Reference chain (U_ref and VAF normalisation)
parameters.relationship: V_p = VAF x U_ref needs U_ref at the height, roughness and profile law that normalised the VAF, from the same time base. Eddy3D ABL defaults (10 m, z0 1 m) and City of London (above 100 m, scaled to 120 m) differ; a mismatch scales every probe speed.

parameters.name: Criteria family and exceedance basis
parameters.relationship: Lower allowed exceedance (City Lawson 5% against Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI 20%) -> stricter class for the same wind; limits are used only with their own exceedance basis, averaging, hours and safety criterion.

parameters.name: Gust treatment
parameters.relationship: GEM is the larger of mean and gust/1.85, gust = mean + 3 RMS (Eddy3D: U + g sqrt(2k/3)), so GEM exceeds the mean only where turbulence intensity exceeds about 28%. Isotropic RMS understates streamwise turbulence (recalled, about 20-40%); declare g and an anisotropy factor.

parameters.name: Zone to required class
parameters.relationship: Toronto: Sitting for seating, balconies and terraces; Standing for entrances and bus stops; Walking for sidewalks and laneways. RWDI: walking or strolling suits sidewalks. Stricter intended use -> lower tolerable speed -> more failures.

parameters.name: Number of simulated wind directions
parameters.relationship: Fewer directions -> coarser, less reliable class map. In one case 16 directions reproduced the 64-direction class over 96% of the area, 8 over 92% (called insufficient), 4 over 79%; City of London requires 36.

parameters.name: Season and governing season
parameters.relationship: The worst season sets the verdict, but which season governs Vancouver must be read from the M01 wind rose; Ontario statements about winter and spring do not transfer. Hamilton accepts some winter degradation as outdoor use falls.

parameters.name: Probe density and placement
parameters.relationship: Sparser probes can miss corner and entrance hot spots; Toronto and Hamilton expect probes about every 10 m along frontages and at least about 50 locations; City of London asks for about 3 probes at each corner.

parameters.name: Cycle routes
parameters.relationship: City of London asks at least one probe every 40 m on cycling paths and applies the 15 m/s safety limit to cyclists; Hamilton lists bicycle lanes as test locations under its pedestrian criteria; Toronto's guide has no cyclist text. Cross-wind gusts at corners are the concern.

parameters.name: Time base of the series
parameters.relationship: ProbeWindSeries is built per time base from the matching WindClimate and M06 refuses mixed tags or time zones. TMYx under-represents storms, so classes from it are labelled typical-year, not 30-year statistics.

metrics.name: Reference-chain gate
metrics.good: VAF reference equals the U_ref reference, time-base and time-zone tags match, inflow profile declared, or a logged conversion is applied
metrics.bad: Mismatched or missing reference, time base or inflow declaration: classification refused
metrics.method: Compare ReferenceSpec fields (z_ref, z0, profile law, averaging time, probe height) and tags
metrics.basis: City of London: reference at a height and location unaffected by the models, with scale factors 0.96-1.48; Toronto 6.4.4: terrain-corrected, gradient-height-scaled data

metrics.name: Homogeneity report present (replaces the 1.5 m empty-domain test)
metrics.good: Empty-domain run shows U, k and epsilon at the building position within the stated tolerance of the inlet profile at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H
metrics.bad: No report, or a pass claimed at 1.5 m only with z0 = 1 m
metrics.method: Read the homogeneity report from M05 or the import template; refuse if absent
metrics.basis: The earlier test (probe at 1.5 m within 5% with Eddy3D defaults) is ill-posed: 1.5 m lies in the roughness sublayer when z0 = 1 m and the standard rough wall function would need cells about 20 m high (Blocken et al. 2007, recalled); tolerances are editable

metrics.name: Calm hours kept in the denominator
metrics.good: Exceedance fractions use every hour of the CriteriaSet window, calm hours included (V = 0, never exceeding)
metrics.bad: Calm hours dropped as missing: E becomes E/(1 - calm share), for example a true 17.6% reads 20.0% at a 12.1% calm share
metrics.method: Denominator = all hours in the season window; log the calm share beside each class
metrics.basis: Arithmetic on the calm shares measured in the ECCC YVR CSVs (12.1% Jan 2025, 6.2% year 2000, 3.1% year 2024); the ECCC CSV leaves direction empty on calm hours, so a naive parser drops them

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (Toronto 2022, three classes)
metrics.good: GEM at or below the zone limit for at least 80% of 06:00-23:00 hours: Sitting 10, Standing 15, Walking 20 km/h
metrics.bad: GEM above 20 km/h for more than 20% of hours (Uncomfortable), or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: Exceedance of the hourly GEM series per season (four seasons)
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR Table 3; earlier label 'RWDI/Toronto' merged two different sets and is corrected

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (Hamilton 2026, four classes)
metrics.good: Sitting under 10, Standing under 14, Strolling under 17, Walking under 20 km/h at 80% occurrence, two seasons (May-Oct, Nov-Apr)
metrics.bad: Over 20 km/h (Uncomfortable)
metrics.method: As above with Hamilton limits and two seasons
metrics.basis: Hamilton Table 1, last updated 20 Feb 2026

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (RWDI, mph)
metrics.good: GEM at or below 6 (Sitting), 8 (Standing), 10 (Strolling), 12 mph (Walking), i.e. about 9.7/12.9/16.1/19.3 km/h, at 20% exceedance, 06:00-23:00
metrics.bad: Above 12 mph (Uncomfortable) or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: As above with RWDI limits; summer May-Oct, winter Nov-Apr
metrics.basis: RWDI Cambridge report criteria table; not identical to Hamilton's 14 and 17 km/h

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (City Lawson, London 2019)
metrics.good: Mean and GEM at or below 2.5 (Frequent Sitting), 4 (Occasional Sitting), 6 (Standing), 8 m/s (Walking) for 95% of all hours; the worse of mean and GEM governs; only the thresholds transfer, not London's climate coefficients
metrics.bad: Above 8 m/s (Uncomfortable), class worse than the zone requires, or the 06:00-23:00 window applied
metrics.method: Exceedance at the 5% level on both series over 24 h data; worst season plus June-August
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 guideline states no comfort-hours window; its Weibull coefficients are explicitly not valid for other areas. The r1 wording 'comfort hours' (06:00-23:00) is corrected

metrics.name: Lawson, Hagbo 2022 version (mean speed only)
metrics.good: Mean speed at or below 4 (Sitting), 6 (Standing), 8 (Strolling), 10 m/s (Business walking) for at most 5% of hours; comfort only
metrics.bad: Safety reported from this set, or described as a GEM set
metrics.method: Exceedance at the 5% level on mean speed
metrics.basis: Secondary source: 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, no safety criterion; primary Lawson text not opened

metrics.name: Safety criterion bound to the family
metrics.good: Gust over 90 km/h for no more than 0.1% of 24 h hours (about 9 h/yr) for Toronto, Hamilton, RWDI (56 mph); City Lawson 15 m/s mean and GEM at 0.022% (about 2 h/yr)
metrics.bad: Toronto safety applied to a Lawson run, or a set with no safety limit reporting safety
metrics.method: Read the safety field of the CriteriaSet; compute the annual exceedance on 24 h hours
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3, Hamilton Table 2, RWDI 56 mph, City of London safety table

metrics.name: Low-wind flag
metrics.good: Mean speed under 5 km/h for less than 80% of hours (80% is the example value in the note)
metrics.bad: Mean speed under 5 km/h for 80% or more of hours: low air circulation, possible exhaust build-up and heat in full sun
metrics.method: Share of hours with mean speed below 5 km/h
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3 note 3 refers to wind speeds lower than 5 km/h for the majority of the time (e.g. 80%), not to GEM; the r1 wording is corrected

metrics.name: GEM turbulence input present
metrics.good: Imported or M05 VAFField carries TKE or turbulence intensity per probe, with g (3) and an anisotropy factor in MethodMetadata; RANS-based GEM labelled indicative
metrics.bad: GEM family run on mean speed only without a warning badge (GEM silently collapses to the mean)
metrics.method: Check the turbulence field; block GEM families or apply a declared default turbulence intensity with a warning badge
metrics.basis: Eddy3D computes GEM as U + g x sqrt(2k/3); GEM exceeds the mean only above about 28% turbulence intensity by definition; the anisotropy factor has no sourced value

metrics.name: Significance of change against baseline
metrics.good: Negligible or beneficial: class unchanged or calmer
metrics.bad: Major adverse: safe becomes unsafe, or suitable becomes unsuitable
metrics.method: Delta of class per probe, existing vs proposed, rated with the City of London scheme
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 significance tables; Hamilton: improve where possible, no significant degradation, winter allowance

metrics.name: Sidewalk required class
metrics.good: Walking at least; Strolling preferred where the set has it
metrics.bad: Uncomfortable on a sidewalk, or Sitting demanded of all sidewalks
metrics.method: Zone map in the CriteriaSet
metrics.basis: RWDI says walking or strolling suits sidewalks; the earlier wording 'strolling or better' is corrected

metrics.name: Cycle-route check
metrics.good: Probe at least every 40 m along cycle routes; mean and GEM below 15 m/s at 0.022% (City Lawson safety limit, applied to cyclists); under Hamilton the pedestrian classes apply to bicycle lanes
metrics.bad: Exceedance of the safety limit at any cycling location, or no probes on cycle routes
metrics.method: Place probes along routes from Layer 0; compute the annual exceedance on 24 h data
metrics.basis: City of London: the 15 m/s safety limit applies to cyclists and tunnel probes are at least every 40 m on cycling paths. Corrected in r3: Hamilton names bicycle lanes as test locations under its standard criteria; Toronto's guide has no cyclist text; use of the London limit with Toronto or Hamilton families is a team choice

metrics.name: Mixed criteria check
metrics.good: One family per run (speed limits with their own exceedance basis, averaging, hours and safety)
metrics.bad: Lawson speeds applied at 20% or RWDI speeds at 5%
metrics.method: Validate CriteriaSet consistency before classification
metrics.basis: Assumption that Lawson and RWDI limits are interchangeable is corrected: bases differ

modules.method: Gates: stop if the VAFField ReferenceSpec, time-base tag or time zone differs from the WindClimate's (unless a logged transfer applies) or if the inflow declaration and homogeneity report are missing. For each probe p and hour h: V_p(h) = VAF_p(theta_h) x U_ref(h), interpolating between the two nearest simulated directions (Eddy3D: Interpolate or Nearest); calm hours give V = 0. Gust = mean + g x RMS (g = 3), RMS from TKE or turbulence intensity with the declared anisotropy factor; GEM = max(mean, gust/1.85); without turbulence data GEM families are blocked or flagged. Per season and the family's hours (in LST), take the best class whose exceedance fraction, over all hours including calms, is within the family's allowance (20% or 5%). Safety: share of 24 h hours above the family's limit; no safety criterion means no safety output. Compare with the zone requirement, check cycle routes, flag low-wind probes on mean speed, rate change against the existing scenario, print the AnalogCriteriaLabel.
visualization: Four false-colour maps (one per season) on the ground plane at 1.5 m: Sitting, Standing, Walking, Uncomfortable in a colour-blind-safe sequential ramp, plus Strolling or the two Lawson sitting classes when those sets are chosen; every map carries the AnalogCriteriaLabel banner
Black hatched markers for probes violating the safety criterion, labelled indicative below L3; cycle-route probes drawn as diamonds along the route
Per-zone pass/fail badges (entrance, sidewalk, plaza, terrace, cycle route) linked to the clause that sets the limit, and a reference-chain badge (z_ref, z0, time base, time zone, averaging time)

Existing-vs-proposed delta map rated with the City of London significance scheme, and a probe table with GEM, exceedance and class; banner 'No VAFField imported: M03 screening only' when no data are loaded

modules.limits: The classification is only as reliable as its input factors. Steady RANS differed from a wind tunnel by -1% to -35% in mean speed in one benchmark, and RANS turbulence gives indicative GEM only. Airport statistics are assumed spatially uniform after the per-sector transfer. High-trigger rezonings need tunnel evidence for safety. The core release has no VAF engine: without an imported VAFField the UI shows M03 screening only.
modules.human_judgment: Deciding the intended use of each space (for example Sitting at the transit plaza), accepting or arguing an exceedance, and trading wind comfort against program and public-realm goals.

modules.name: Fast wind simulation engine: CFD and surrogates
modules.effort: v1 scope: XS (1-2 days) Eddy3D/tunnel workflow guide and import template feeding M04; M (5-7 days) documented OpenFOAM-12 L2-lite case template (capped tabulated inflow, rough-wall set-up, homogeneity test) run offline, plus 1 day to time one direction on target hardware before L2-lite is offered. Hosted pipeline and L2-full: L (3-5 person-weeks), roadmap
modules.design_question: How should the tool produce directional velocity amplification factors for a massing quickly, on a stated reference and inflow, at what fidelity and compute cost, and how is accuracy declared?
inputs: Layer 0 mesh (STL/OBJ) of the scheme plus context to the ContextSpec radius, at least max(400 m, about 2H); features over 0.5 m near pedestrian zones modelled; vegetation excluded from baseline
Approved and future towers as a required cumulative context scenario, plus influential taller towers beyond the radius when upwind
Wind sectors and the per-sector ReferenceSpec from M01 (approach z0 per direction, gradient height)
ProbeSet and priority probes from M03
Inflow profile choice (Deaves-Harris/ESDU or log law capped at gradient height) tabulated for U, k and epsilon, and top boundary type
Fidelity level selected by the user
outputs: VAFField: probe x direction speed ratios with ReferenceSpec (reference height, approach z0, profile law, gradient height, probe height), inflow declaration up to at least 1.2 H, top boundary type, optionally turbulent kinetic energy

MethodMetadata: code and version, mesh and cell count, turbulence model, wall treatment, domain size in H and blockage ratio, homogeneity report, core-hours (measured or labelled order of magnitude), validation case, fidelity label, uncertainty tag
FlowViz meshes: streamlines, vertical slices

parameters.name: Proximity model radius
parameters.relationship: Toronto asks about 350 m, Hamilton and City of London 400 m, plus influential taller buildings beyond. That is only about 1.1-1.6 tower heights for 244-305 m towers; a larger radius capturing upwind towers -> truer approach flow and wakes.

parameters.name: Domain size relative to H
parameters.relationship: AIJ practice as reported: 6 Hmax high (5 above the tallest building), 15 Hmax downstream, blockage at most 3%; Hagbo used 6 H and 15 H. At H = 305 m that is about 1.8 km high and 6 km long. Smaller domains raise blockage, so it is logged.

parameters.name: Number of wind directions
parameters.relationship: Toronto requires at least 16 for CFD and 36 for tunnel; City of London 36 for all studies; Hamilton CFD may use prevailing directions only, weighted over all directions. Fewer directions -> coarser classes (79% same class with 4, 96% with 16, by area, one case).

parameters.name: Turbulence model and steadiness
parameters.relationship: Steady RANS tends to overpredict high-speed areas and underpredict wakes against a tunnel; Toronto accepts two-equation RANS or LES; City of London avoids standard k-epsilon, calls realisable k-epsilon the robust standard and allows k-omega SST on a suitable mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh and probe height
parameters.relationship: City of London asks 0.3 m cells near entrances and corners, 10 cells across a canyon, 3 prism layers below 1.5 m and modelled features over 0.5 m near pedestrians; Toronto ignores under 1 m. Coarser near-ground mesh -> poorer 1.5 m speeds.

parameters.name: Reference and inflow profile
parameters.relationship: VAF depends on where U_ref is defined: Eddy3D ABL defaults to 10 m, 5 m/s and z0 1 m with a log law; City of London wants a reference above 100 m clear of the model. OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer is an uncapped log law.

parameters.name: Inflow profile cap and top boundary
parameters.relationship: Tower-top speed drives downwash, so inflow must stay physical to about 1.2 H: capped at gradient height with a consistent top condition. atmBoundaryLayer cannot cap; a tabulated fixedProfile inlet (U, k, epsilon against height, clamped above gradient height) can. Hagbo used a log law with a slip top.

parameters.name: Ground roughness and wall function
parameters.relationship: A standard rough wall function turns z0 = 1 m into a sand-grain height near 20 m (Blocken 2007, recalled), incompatible with 0.3 m cells. Use an atmospheric rough wall function for the approach fetch and a small z0 where buildings are explicit.

parameters.name: Fidelity level
parameters.relationship: Rules (M03) -> ML surrogate -> RANS lite -> RANS full -> wind tunnel: gust reliability rises, speed falls. Surrogate vendors claim seconds to minutes; independent accuracy for supertall downtown contexts is not verified.

parameters.name: Compute budget
parameters.relationship: One laboratory case (OpenFOAM 4.1 in Docker on Windows, one 2018 core, 3 non-orthogonal correctors, residuals to 1e-5) took 15 h 10 min for 0.26 M cells, about 57 core-hours per million cells. Linear scaling gives roughly 1,800-4,600 core-hours for 2-5 M cells x 16 directions: an order of magnitude, not a bound.

parameters.name: Context scenario
parameters.relationship: Existing plus approved towers change upwind sheltering and channelling; Toronto models projects approved in the last 5 years, City of London consented schemes, Hamilton future cases only if warranted. The VTC brief names future approved towers, so the cumulative case is required.

metrics.name: Directions simulated
metrics.good: At least 16 equal sectors for CFD (Toronto); 36 for tunnel (Toronto, Hamilton) and for any City of London study
metrics.bad: Fewer than 16 for CFD; Hamilton's prevailing-only CFD is accepted by Hamilton but fails Toronto
metrics.method: Check run metadata
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.2 and 6.4.3; Hamilton Technical Requirement 1.A allows prevailing directions for qualitative CFD and 1.B requires 36 for tunnel; City of London 36. The earlier claim that both cities require 16 CFD directions is corrected

metrics.name: Modelled context radius
metrics.good: At least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond it
metrics.bad: 350 m or less, or no upwind towers beyond the radius
metrics.method: Measure from site boundary to the domain context edge; list added towers
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.1: 350 m is a minimum and tall buildings outside it that could influence the site must be included; Hamilton and City of London 400 m; the 2H term is a team assumption

metrics.name: ReferenceSpec on the VAFField
metrics.good: Reference height, approach z0, profile law and probe height declared
metrics.bad: Reference missing: M04 refuses the field
metrics.method: Schema check on the VAFField
metrics.basis: City of London requires a stated reference; Eddy3D's VAF page names no reference height, so users must copy their ABL settings

metrics.name: Inflow profile and top boundary declared
metrics.good: Profile capped at gradient height, tabulated (fixedProfile inlet with out-of-bounds clamp for U, k and epsilon) and declared up to at least 1.2 H; top condition consistent with it (prescribed shear stress or fixed U, k, epsilon, per Richards and Hoxey, recalled)
metrics.bad: Uncapped log law to the domain top with an undeclared top condition, or a profile declared only near the ground
metrics.method: Read the inlet files and compare the profile at 1.2 H with the declared law; refuse the VAFField if absent; include the tabulated inlet in the homogeneity run
metrics.basis: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer is an uncapped log law (S50); the fixedProfile boundary condition exists in the OpenFOAM-12 source with a Function1 table and clamping (S54, header read, not run in a case); k and epsilon consistent with a capped U are not sourced; City of London names Harris-Deaves/ESDU 01008; the 1.2 H and Richards-Hoxey choices are team and recalled

metrics.name: Horizontal homogeneity of the empty domain
metrics.good: U, k and epsilon at the building position within the stated tolerance of the inlet profile at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H (placeholder 5% on U)
metrics.bad: Profile decays along the domain, or a pass shown only at 1.5 m
metrics.method: Run the domain without buildings and compare profiles at the future building position with the inlet
metrics.basis: Replaces the 1.5 m empty-domain test; Blocken et al. 2007 on wall-function inhomogeneity (recalled, not opened); tolerance is a team placeholder

metrics.name: Ground roughness and wall-function consistency
metrics.good: Approach ground uses an atmospheric rough wall function (nutkAtmRoughWallFunction) with z0 equal to the inlet z0; wall-adjacent cell centre above the equivalent sand-grain height or the exception logged; small z0 (placeholder 0.01-0.05 m) on explicitly modelled ground
metrics.bad: z0 = 1 m on a ground with 0.3 m cells, or the same large z0 counted again where buildings are explicit
metrics.method: Inspect boundary-condition files and first-cell heights
metrics.basis: nutkAtmRoughWallFunction exists in OpenFOAM-12 and is meant for use with atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity; the sand-grain relation is recalled from Blocken 2007; Hagbo used z0 = 3 m on terrain with 0.68 m cells, so published practice differs; the small-z0 range is the critic's recommendation

metrics.name: Fidelity and compute label
metrics.good: Each map carries its level (L1 screening, L2-lite comparative only, L2-full) with cell count and core-hours; core-hours are labelled 'order of magnitude, one laboratory case (S49)' until a benchmark on the target hardware exists
metrics.bad: Unlabelled map, L2-lite results presented as compliance evidence, or the 57 core-hours per million cells called a lower bound
metrics.method: Write the level, cell count and core-hours to MethodMetadata and show the label on every map
metrics.basis: Corrected in r3: the S49 case is a 0.26 M cell laboratory box run with OpenFOAM 4.1 in Docker on Windows at 16 s per iteration (61 s per million cells per iteration), so the extrapolation is neither a lower nor an upper bound; 2-5 M cells for L2-lite and tens of millions for L2-full are team assumptions

metrics.name: L2-lite benchmark gate
metrics.good: One direction of the L2-lite template run and timed on the target hardware before L2-lite is offered to entrants; cells, iterations, residual targets, cores and wall time logged and the budget re-derived
metrics.bad: L2-lite offered on the extrapolated figure alone (about 1,800-4,600 core-hours would not fit a laptop before 30 Nov)
metrics.method: Run direction 1 of 16 on the target machine; multiply by directions; publish the measured figure
metrics.basis: Process gate from the r3 critique; no measured supertall-scale run exists; S49 gives the only data point and its own 3,000-iteration extrapolation (13.3 h box, 17.5 h cylindrical for 0.26 M cells)

metrics.name: Decision-level validation against tunnel data
metrics.good: Class agreement with tunnel data at or above a team-set level (placeholder 80% of probes) and exceedance-probability bias within a team-set band (placeholder 5 percentage points), on AIJ cases
metrics.bad: Outside these bands, or no benchmark run; r and FAC2 alone presented as validation
metrics.method: Run the benchmark; compare comfort class and exceedance fraction at each probe against tunnel data; report with the VDI 3783-9 hit rate once opened
metrics.basis: Replaces FAC2 >= 0.5, |FB| <= 0.3, NMSE <= 4 from dispersion practice, which tolerate class-shifting speed errors; AIJ cases to run: the Niigata case E (Hagbo) plus a single tall building and a tall building among low-rise blocks (recalled, case identities to confirm); no supertall benchmark found

metrics.name: Descriptive statistics (FAC2, FB, NMSE)
metrics.good: Reported alongside, with no acceptance band adopted
metrics.bad: Used as pass/fail with bands taken from dispersion-model evaluation
metrics.method: Compute at benchmark probes
metrics.basis: Chang and Hanna 2004 bands were recalled differently in r1 and r2 (NMSE below 4 versus about 1.5) and not opened

metrics.name: Hit rate against reference data (COST 732 / VDI 3783-9 style)
metrics.good: 66% or higher (recalled, to confirm)
metrics.bad: Below 66%
metrics.method: Fraction of probes within stated tolerance of the reference
metrics.basis: Recalled from COST 732/VDI practice; Toronto only cites COST 732 as the guideline to follow; originals not opened

metrics.name: Agreement with wind-tunnel benchmark (Pearson r)
metrics.good: Report r per direction as supplementary information only
metrics.bad: Used as pass/fail: r is scale-invariant and would pass a model that underpredicts speeds by 35%
metrics.method: Correlation of CFD vs tunnel at probes for an AIJ benchmark
metrics.basis: Hagbo and Giljarhus Table 5: r 0.61 (247.5 deg) to 0.84 (180 deg), text says 0.71-0.84; mean speed differences -1% to -35%. The earlier 0.71-0.84 pass/fail band is corrected

metrics.name: Domain and blockage logged
metrics.good: Domain 6 Hmax high (5 above the tallest building), 15 Hmax downstream and blockage at most 3%, or the departure logged, in MethodMetadata
metrics.bad: Not logged
metrics.method: Compute from the case files
metrics.basis: Two peer-reviewed papers (S49, S06) quote the AIJ and COST 732 domain rules; the AIJ and COST 732 originals were not opened; whether the rules suffice for 305 m towers is unverified

metrics.name: Geometry detail near pedestrian zones
metrics.good: Features projecting more than 0.5 m modelled near pedestrian areas; under 1 m ignored elsewhere
metrics.bad: Entrance and corner detail removed
metrics.method: Check the mesh geometry against the Layer 0 detail list
metrics.basis: City of London requires features over 0.5 m near pedestrian areas; Toronto says dimensions under 1 m have no notable impact; the stricter rule applies near pedestrians

metrics.name: Solver version pinned
metrics.good: OpenFOAM Foundation v12 pinned for Eddy3D compatibility (it contains atmBoundaryLayer, nutkAtmRoughWallFunction and fixedProfile), or v13 after re-test; version in MethodMetadata
metrics.bad: Unpinned or silently upgraded
metrics.method: Read the container tag
metrics.basis: Eddy3D uses OpenFOAM 12; the atmospheric boundary conditions and fixedProfile were read in the OpenFOAM-12 source; Foundation v13 repository exists

metrics.name: Surrogate accuracy claim
metrics.good: Independently validated for supertall, dense downtown contexts
metrics.bad: Vendor claim only (for example 90%+ accuracy)
metrics.method: Run the surrogate and RANS on the same massing and compare
metrics.basis: Vendor statements; no independent validation opened

modules.method: Fidelity ladder. L0: M03 rules. L1: ML surrogate (Eddy3D Wind Predictor, GAN surrogate, Infrared.city API), screening only. L2-lite: OpenFOAM-12 steady RANS, comparative only, offered only after the benchmark gate: context to max(400 m, about 2H) plus approved towers; rotating cylindrical domain meshed once (6 Hmax high, 15 Hmax downstream, blockage at most 3%); tabulated fixedProfile inflow capped at gradient height with a consistent top condition; atmospheric rough wall upstream and small z0 on modelled ground; empty-domain homogeneity run; 1-2 m cells at probes (placeholder), about 2-5 M cells, 16 directions. L2-full: City of London mesh (0.3 m cells, 10 cells per canyon, prism layers), 16-36 directions, cluster or consultant. L3: consultant tunnel study (36 directions, about 50 probes). Validate on AIJ cases by class agreement and exceedance bias. M04 reads any VAFField, including imported CSV.
visualization: Contour map of VAF at 1.5 m per direction, diverging colour ramp centred on 1.0 (legend 0-2, editable), with streamlines
Vertical slice through the tower and podium at the worst corner
Residual and convergence plots for L2 runs, plus profile plots of U, k and epsilon (inlet versus building position) for the homogeneity run

Confusion matrix of comfort classes (CFD vs reference) with percent agreement, and a fidelity badge reading 'L1 screening only', 'L2-lite comparative only' or 'L2-full' with cell count and core-hours (measured, or labelled order of magnitude)
