modules.limits: CFD at massing stage cannot reliably predict gusts, flow separation or safety exceedances (Toronto). Steady RANS shows bias against tunnels. Surrogates have undisclosed training domains. L2-full is a cluster or consultant task; L2-lite is comparative only and its cost is unmeasured. No supertall benchmark was found: AIJ case E has a 60 m high-rise. Eddy3D needs Rhino 8, so a web tool imports its results or runs its own OpenFOAM service.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the fidelity level, judging mesh quality and validation, deciding when a consultant wind-tunnel study is warranted, and signing off any safety conclusion.

modules.name: Outdoor thermal comfort and rain exposure
modules.effort: M: 6-8 person-days (UTCI engine, clamping and counters, time-base and time-zone tag check, MRT input from the sun/shade module, two-station rain composite, driving-rain index, category maps)
modules.design_question: In which public spaces and seasons do wind, sun, temperature and rain give acceptable outdoor comfort, and where does tower-induced wind or canopy cover help or hurt?
inputs: WindClimate[time base] with concurrent temperature and humidity (concurrent-30y or TMYx); the choice is stored in MethodMetadata
ProbeWindSeries (mean speed series) from M04 on the same time-base and time-zone tags
Mean radiant temperature series from the sun/shadow module (other packet); fallback ladybug-comfort solar-adjusted MRT, labelled approximate

Hourly precipitation: for the 30-year base, ECCC Vancouver Harbour CS hourly precipitation (present in sampled months 2010-2026, 13.0 km from YVR) joined to YVR wind on concurrent UTC hours as a logged two-station composite; for the TMYx base, the EPW liquid-precipitation field (origin unverified). The YVR hourly precipitation column is empty (0 of 8,784 hours in 2024)
CanopyCoverageTable from M03 and M07, zone tags and occupancy hours
outputs: UTCIMap: per probe and hour, UTCI and stress category with a validity flag (valid, clipped-calm, storm-excluded, out-of-range)
ThermalComfortSummary per zone and season, with excluded-hour counts
WindHelpsOrHurts flag per zone
RainExposureIndex per frontage and sector (with rain-input coverage and source on the badge), and WeatherProtectionCoverage per frontage

parameters.name: Pedestrian-level mean wind speed
parameters.relationship: Higher wind lowers UTCI: relief in heat, added cold stress in cold. This tool feeds mean speed, not GEM (team choice). Calm (mean under 5 km/h most of the time) in full sun risks poor circulation, so Sitting-class wind is not automatically thermally good.

parameters.name: Mean radiant temperature (sun and shade)
parameters.relationship: Shade from tower, podium or trees lowers Tmrt -> lower UTCI in summer, but also removes winter solar gain. Tmrt minus air temperature must stay within -30 to +70 K for valid UTCI.

parameters.name: Air temperature and humidity
parameters.relationship: UTCI is the equivalent air temperature of a reference environment (50% RH with vapour pressure capped at 20 hPa, calm air, radiant temperature equal to air temperature); valid for air temperature -50 to 50 C and vapour pressure up to 5 kPa.

parameters.name: Wind reference conversion to 10 m
parameters.relationship: UTCI expects 10 m wind. Ladybug says 10 m speed is 1.5 times the speed at ground; a log law with z0 = 0.01 m (recalled) gives ln(10/0.01)/ln(h/0.01): 1.47 at 1.1 m, 1.38 at 1.5 m. Unscaled pedestrian speed -> cold stress understated.

parameters.name: Activity and clothing assumption
parameters.relationship: UTCI assumes walking at about 2.4 met with adaptive clothing; seated plaza users fall outside the assumption and the docs suggest PET for such cases, so sitting-zone results are less certain.

parameters.name: Time base and concurrency
parameters.relationship: A typical-year file is internally consistent but under-represents storms; a 30-year record keeps temperature, humidity and wind concurrent (Arctic outflow, 1-3 times per winter) but has no concurrent solar. M06 refuses inputs whose time-base or time-zone tags differ.

parameters.name: Input clamping and exclusion
parameters.relationship: pythermalcomfort returns NaN below 0.5 or above 17 m/s (the official program accepts up to 30 m/s but documents 17). Clipping sheltered hours to 0.5 m/s and counting storm hours keeps calm zones in the denominator; dropping them biases shares.

parameters.name: Wind-driven rain exposure
parameters.relationship: Rain falling with wind from a sector slants onto frontages facing it; stronger wind and wider windward frontage -> more wetted pedestrian area. Magnitude not quantified; a driving-rain index (ISO 15927-3) is a candidate, not opened. A two-station composite adds timing and exposure error.

parameters.name: Weather-protection coverage
parameters.relationship: Continuous deep canopies and covered walkways shelter pedestrians from rain and, per Toronto and Hamilton, deflect downwash at the base. Coverage targets in Vancouver guidance were not opened.

metrics.name: UTCI category
metrics.good: 9 to 26 deg C: no thermal stress
metrics.bad: Above 32 (strong heat stress, up to extreme above 46) or below -13 (strong cold stress, down to extreme below -40)
metrics.method: Classify each hourly UTCI with thresholds 46/38/32/26(28)/9/0/-13/-27/-40; Ladybug splits 26-32 at 28 into slight and moderate heat stress
metrics.basis: Ladybug-comfort default thresholds implementing the Broede et al. scale; scale itself not opened

metrics.name: Input validity
metrics.good: 10 m wind 0.5-17 m/s; air temperature -50 to 50 C; Tr minus Ta -30 to 70 K; RH 0-100%; vapour pressure 0-5 kPa
metrics.bad: Outside range: result is NaN or unrealistic if extrapolated; UTCI can also be non-monotonic in wind speed
metrics.method: Enforce limit_inputs in pythermalcomfort
metrics.basis: pythermalcomfort documentation

metrics.name: Clamping rule and excluded hours
metrics.good: Calm hours clipped to 0.5 m/s; hours above 17 m/s or otherwise out of range counted per probe and shown as a separate class; shares use all occupied hours
metrics.bad: NaN hours silently dropped from the denominator
metrics.method: Counters per probe and season; show valid and excluded hours side by side
metrics.basis: Editable rule built on the documented validity limits; the 0.5 m/s clip is a team choice

metrics.name: Time base declared and matched
metrics.good: Concurrent temperature, humidity and wind from one record, or all variables from one TMYx year; the same time-base and time-zone tag on WindClimate, ProbeWindSeries and Tmrt; label shown on every map
metrics.bad: Typical-year temperature with a 30-year wind record, or any input with a different tag
metrics.method: Check the time-base and time-zone tag of every input series; refuse to merge differing tags (schema check)
metrics.basis: Design rule; default is TMYx because solar is needed; M01 and M04 emit a series per time base so the default has a consistent wind input; TMYx origin per hour is unverified ('NCEI ISD/ERA5')

metrics.name: Share of occupied hours with no thermal stress
metrics.good: At least 50% of occupied hours in 9-26 C (editable placeholder)
metrics.bad: Below 25% of occupied hours (editable placeholder)
metrics.method: Count hours per zone in each UTCI category
metrics.basis: No sourced target; team to set per space type

metrics.name: Ground-to-10 m wind conversion
metrics.good: Factor computed from the declared probe height h as ln(10/z0)/ln(h/z0) with z0 = 0.01 m (about 1.38 at 1.5 m), sensitivity band shown
metrics.bad: Unscaled pedestrian speed fed into UTCI, or an undocumented factor
metrics.method: Compute the factor from the probe height; show a sensitivity band
metrics.basis: Ladybug states a 1.5 factor attributed to the Fiala model; the log-law form with z0 = 0.01 m and body height 1.1 m (factor 1.47) is recalled from the UTCI procedure, whose primary text was not opened

metrics.name: Rain input coverage
metrics.good: Badge shows the share of hours with hourly precipitation, the source (Harbour CS composite or EPW field) and the 13.0 km station separation; EPW precipitation labelled 'origin unverified'
metrics.bad: YVR hourly precipitation assumed present, or the composite hidden
metrics.method: Count populated precipitation hours per source and season; join on UTC; show both
metrics.basis: ECCC YVR hourly precipitation is empty in every sampled month (0 of 8,784 hours in 2024); ISD AA1 holds only 3 h and 6 h synoptic accumulations; Harbour CS hourly precipitation is populated in sampled months 2010-2026 (738-744 of 744 hours). The YVR TMYx precipitation field sums to 1,795 mm, against 957.6 mm measured at YVR in 2025 (ECCC daily), so its bias is unquantified

metrics.name: Weather-protection coverage
metrics.good: Higher share of retail and transit-plaza frontage under canopy than the baseline scheme
metrics.bad: Lower share than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Canopy footprint along each frontage divided by frontage length
metrics.basis: No sourced target; City of Vancouver weather-protection guidance not opened

metrics.name: Driving-rain exposure
metrics.good: Smaller wetted frontage length than the baseline scheme
metrics.bad: Larger wetted frontage length than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Weight hourly rain by wind direction and frontage orientation, reduced by canopy coverage
metrics.basis: Candidate method ISO 15927-3 not opened; no Vancouver threshold found

modules.method: Choose a time base: B) one TMYx year for all variables (default), or A) concurrent 30-year ECCC/ISD temperature, humidity and wind with Tmrt from the sun/shade module (cold-stress screening, no concurrent solar). Per probe and hour: air temperature and humidity from that base; mean pedestrian wind from M04 on the same base, converted to the UTCI 10 m convention with ln(10/z0)/ln(h/z0) (z0 default 0.01 m, h the probe height, editable), clipped to 0.5 m/s, excluded above 17 m/s and counted; Tmrt from the sun/shadow module. Compute UTCI with the Broede polynomial via pythermalcomfort with limits on; classify with the 10-threshold scale. Aggregate per zone and season over occupancy hours, excluded hours as their own class. Flag zones where wind moves the category versus a calm baseline. Rain: weight hourly precipitation (composite or EPW field, coverage shown) by wind direction and frontage orientation and compare with canopy coverage.
visualization: Ground-plane false-colour map of percent of occupied hours in 'no thermal stress' (0-100%), seasonal toggle, with a grey excluded-hours overlay
Calendar heat map (day x hour) for a selected probe coloured by the UTCI scale (-40 to 46 C, diverging blue-white-red)
Stacked bars per zone of hours in each stress category plus a grey 'excluded' segment
Wind-effect arrow chips per zone (helps/hurts)
Plan of frontage lines coloured by driving-rain index (0-1), hatched where canopy coverage exists, with a rain-source badge

modules.limits: UTCI is an outdoor index; Tmrt needs a radiation model beyond Layer 0, and trees and surfaces ('City in Nature') are not modelled by default. The 10 m wind conversion rests on a recalled log-law form and UTCI can be non-monotonic in wind speed. A typical year under-represents Vancouver heat events and cold snaps; no future climate files applied. Rain comes from a two-station composite or an EPW field of unverified origin; the rain method and weather-protection targets are unverified.
modules.human_judgment: Setting the acceptable stress level per space type, trading summer shade against winter sun, judging comfort for seated and children's uses outside the UTCI activity assumption, and deciding how much rain cover the public realm needs.
depends_on: EXT: Tmrt series from the sun/shadow module (other packet, id to be assigned; fallback ladybug-comfort MRT)

modules.name: Wind mitigation comparison and advisor
modules.effort: M: 5-7 person-days (scenario graph, delta maps, ordered mitigation library, significance scheme, vegetation rule)
modules.design_question: Which design changes reduce wind exceedances most, tried in order of large-scale massing first, then architectural details, then localised screens, and what does each cost the design?
inputs: ComfortMap scenarios: existing, proposed, mitigation, phasing (each with its AnalogCriteriaLabel)
WindRiskField from M03
Geometry change log from Layer 0
Program and floor-area data
Vegetation objects (trees, planting) with declared leaf area density and foliage state, used only in mitigation scenarios
outputs: MitigationScenarioSet
DeltaComfortMap (scenario minus baseline) with City of London significance classes and the analog label
RankedMitigations (3-tier order)
SignificantChangeLog: which edits require re-running M05
CanopyCoverageUpdate (to M06)

parameters.name: Orientation, siting and massing changes
parameters.relationship: Largest area of influence: building shape, height, podium and corner changes alter flow over the whole frontage; Toronto instructs applicants to try these first, before details or screens.

parameters.name: Canopies, recessed entrances, base articulation
parameters.relationship: Local mitigation at entrances and walkways; deep and wrap-around canopies redirect downwash away from ground and add rain cover (M06). Effect is confined to a small area and applied after massing options are exhausted.

parameters.name: Wind screens and landscaping
parameters.relationship: Screens at least 6 ft (about 1.8 m) tall and 20-40% porous diffused corner winds in one RWDI project; Toronto requires written City approval to rely on them, and landscaping must be effective at installation.

parameters.name: Vegetation in baseline versus mitigation scenarios
parameters.relationship: Toronto does not consider landscaping unless agreed with the City; City of London ignores landscape under 8 m in baselines. A 'City in Nature' scheme taking planting credit in massing runs would understate wind; trees enter only mitigation scenarios.

parameters.name: Construction phasing
parameters.relationship: Interim phases before later buildings arrive can be windier than the final scheme, so phased projects need separate scenarios.

parameters.name: Significant design changes
parameters.relationship: Changes in building count, orientation, setback, massing, height, tower offset from podium or canopies can alter wind enough to require a new study; any such edit marks results stale.

parameters.name: Significance of a class shift
parameters.relationship: City of London rates a change by class shift: windier by one class but still suitable is moderate adverse; safe becoming unsafe or suitable becoming unsuitable is major adverse. This replaces an undefined 'significant degradation'.

metrics.name: Net effect against existing conditions
metrics.good: Improves existing conditions where possible; no probe worsens by a class
metrics.bad: Major adverse: safe becomes unsafe or suitable becomes unsuitable (City of London); Hamilton: significant degradation, especially of safety
metrics.method: Delta ComfortMap per zone and season rated with the City of London scheme
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 significance tables; Hamilton assessment text

metrics.name: Mitigation order followed
metrics.good: Massing first, architectural details second, localised features third
metrics.bad: Screens or trees used to rescue an unmitigated massing
metrics.method: Check the mitigation scenario history
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.7.2 prioritisation

metrics.name: Vegetation excluded from baseline
metrics.good: No vegetation in Existing and Proposed baseline runs (landscape under 8 m ignored); trees only in mitigation scenarios, declared with leaf area density and foliage state and flagged as dependent on City approval
metrics.bad: Planting credited in massing or baseline runs
metrics.method: Check scenario objects against the vegetation rule
metrics.basis: Toronto: landscaping not considered unless agreed with the City; City of London: ignore landscape elements under 8 m in baseline studies; leaf area density values are unsourced

metrics.name: Significant-change trigger
metrics.good: No change in the Toronto 6.2 list since the last run
metrics.bad: Any listed change marks M04 results stale
metrics.method: Classify each Layer 0 edit against the list
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.2 significant design changes

metrics.name: Wind-screen specification
metrics.good: At least 1.8 m tall and 20-40% porous, confirmed by an M05 or tunnel re-run
metrics.bad: Lower or solid screens, or credit taken without a re-run
metrics.method: Check screen objects in the mitigation scenario and the re-run record
metrics.basis: One RWDI project recommendation (Cambridge MA 2021), not a standard; Toronto requires written City approval to rely on screens

modules.method: Maintain a scenario graph (Existing, Proposed, Mitigation A..n, Phase n). Baseline and massing scenarios exclude vegetation; trees enter only mitigation scenarios as porous media with declared leaf area density and foliage state, flagged approval-dependent. Each edit to Layer 0 is classified against the Toronto significant-change list and marks M04 results stale. For each scenario pair compute per-probe change in class and in exceedance fraction, rate it with the City of London significance scheme, and compute the area of public realm moved into or out of the required class. Rank candidate mitigations by tier (massing, architectural, localised) and by area improved, using results from re-runs rather than assumed effectiveness. The library stores sourced notes (screens at least 1.8 m tall and 20-40% porous, wrap-around corner canopies, podium step-backs) as hypotheses with their source project. Output the order, the deltas, the analog label and a reason log for the board text.
visualization: Before/after slider on the ground-plane comfort map
Delta map: blue where class improves, red where it worsens, with safety-class changes outlined in black and significance class in the legend
Ordered list with a tier badge and area improved per option; vegetation options carry an 'approval needed' badge
Pareto scatter: public-realm area meeting target versus floor area or design intent lost

libraries.role: Scenario deltas and ranking (licences not re-verified)

libraries.name: plotly.js / three.js
libraries.role: Slider, delta overlay and Pareto chart

modules.limits: Mitigation effectiveness is project-specific. No general effectiveness coefficients were found, so each option needs a re-run in M05 or a tunnel test. Screens and trees are excluded at massing stage in Toronto-style reviews and need approval. The screen specification comes from one consultant report and is an editable assumption; no sourced leaf area density values exist.
modules.human_judgment: Which trade-off to accept (floor area, form, public programme, trees against wind), design intent and aesthetics, and whether to seek City approval for localised features.

modules.name: Elevated public terrace and sky-lobby wind check
modules.effort: M: about 5 person-days after M05 exists; wind-tunnel confirmation outside tool scope
modules.design_question: Are publicly accessible terraces, sky gardens and podium roofs high in the tower usable for their intended activity in each season, or do they need screens, enclosure or re-siting?
inputs: Layer 0 levels tagged public or amenity at height
VAFField with ReferenceSpec and inflow declaration to at least 1.2 H at terrace probes (CFD or ML roof-level prediction) from M05 or imported
WindClimate
CriteriaSet and AnalogCriteriaLabel (with safety criterion)
Parapet or screen geometry
outputs: TerraceSuitabilityTable per level and season (with the analog label)
RecommendedScreens or enclosure list

Hand-off notes: to P10 (tower height, corner treatment and taper used; no structural calculation here; confirm the current Vancouver Building By-law edition first), to SPAC/P10 (ice and snow shedding zones, unquantified) and to SYST (entrance and below-grade connection drafts, unquantified)

parameters.name: Height above ground
parameters.relationship: Wind speed increases with elevation, so terraces higher in the tower meet stronger wind; the brief's vertically distributed public uses raise exposure. A quantified gradient is not given in the opened sources.

parameters.name: Terrace position on the facade
parameters.relationship: Terrace corners and windward faces receive accelerated and downwashing flow; RWDI used guardrails at least 6 ft tall and wrap-around canopies to cut speeds at exposed terrace corners.

parameters.name: Season of use
parameters.relationship: Summer sitting use needs the calmest class; winter use is lower so Hamilton accepts some winter degradation, which can justify seasonal closure.

parameters.name: Parapet and screen height
parameters.relationship: Taller parapets or porous screens lower speed at terrace level; amount depends on geometry and is not quantified in sources.

parameters.name: Reference profile at terrace height
parameters.relationship: A VAF normalised near 10 m with a log-law inflow may not describe wind at 150-300 m; a wrong profile there scales terrace speeds and classes. Eddy3D ABL and OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer use an uncapped log law; validity aloft is unverified.

metrics.name: Terrace comfort class
metrics.good: Sitting for seating terraces in the season of use (Toronto 10 km/h; City Lawson Occasional Sitting 4 m/s); Standing for circulation
metrics.bad: Walking or Uncomfortable (over 20 km/h at 20% in Toronto) for a space meant for sitting
metrics.method: Reuse the M04 engine with terrace probes
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3 lists balconies and amenity terraces under Sitting; RWDI recommends sitting conditions for terraces and podiums; City of London lists balconies and terraces as Occasional Sitting

metrics.name: Terrace gust safety
metrics.good: Within the safety criterion of the chosen family (Toronto: gust at or below 90 km/h for 0.1% of hours or less; City Lawson: 15 m/s at 0.022%)
metrics.bad: Above the family's limit
metrics.method: 24 h annual exceedance at terrace probes
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3; City of London safety table

metrics.name: Prediction confidence at height
metrics.good: Tunnel-validated
metrics.bad: Unvalidated RANS or surrogate at 100+ m levels
metrics.method: Read MethodMetadata from M05
metrics.basis: No sourced validation of height-level predictions in opened material

modules.method: Select Layer 0 spaces tagged public or amenity above grade. Place probes 1.5 m above the terrace floor on a grid and at corners (City of London lists upper-level terraces and balconies as critical locations). Obtain VAF with ReferenceSpec at those probes from M05 (CFD sampling, or the Eddy3D roof-level ML output when building geometry is supplied), refusing fields whose inflow profile is not declared to terrace height. Run the M04 engine with the terrace-specific required class, season of use and the family's safety criterion, and report class and safety. Where a terrace fails, propose screens (height and porosity from the M07 library), enclosure or relocation to a leeward face, and re-run. Add hand-off notes to P10, SPAC and SYST listing what changed.
visualization: Tower elevation or section with terrace markers coloured by summer and winter class

modules.limits: Prediction at height is the least validated part of this packet; steady RANS and surrogates trained mainly on ground-level probes may not transfer to 150-300 m, and the inflow profile aloft is unverified. sources.title: Pedestrian Level Wind Study Terms of Reference Guide
sources.publisher: City of Toronto, Urban Design, with RWDI
sources.extract: Re-read in r1-r3 (text extracted). Table 1 (Area 1 High over 100 m), Table 2, 3.b shifts; 5.1 scenarios incl. projects approved in last 5 years; 5.3 four seasons; 6.2 significant changes; 6.4.1 proximity radius about 350 m minimum plus tall buildings beyond; 6.4.2 CFD (COST 732, two-equation RANS or LES, 16 directions); 6.4.4 30-year hourly data corrected for terrain and scaled to gradient height (600 m example), comfort 06:00-23:00 and safety 24 h with no time zone stated; Table 3 three classes 10/15/20 km/h at 80%, 90 km/h gust at 0.1%; note 3 concerns wind speed (not GEM) under 5 km/h for the majority of the time (e.g. 80%); landscaping not considered unless agreed with the City; 6.7.2 mitigation order. r3: a text search finds no cyclist or bicycle wording.

sources.title: Development Application Guidelines: Wind Study (last updated 20 February 2026)
sources.extract: Re-read in r1-r3. Triggers (20 m, 44 m, 2x surroundings, 2+ buildings, 3 ha); qualitative CFD may simulate prevailing directions only; tunnel 36 directions, 400 m, sensors every 10 m and about 50 locations; 30 years of hourly data from the airport; Table 1 under 10/14/17/20 km/h at 80%, 06:00-23:00 with no time zone stated; Table 2 90 km/h gust at 0.1%; Summer May-Oct and Winter Nov-Apr although the text says 'four-season basis'; winter allowance. r3: scope defines cyclist areas (frontages, pathways, entrances, open spaces, bicycle parking, bicycle routes); test locations include bicycle lanes adjacent to the building; the Walking class text mentions cycling; no separate cyclist threshold. Adoption status unconfirmed: file name says 'ph1proposed'.

sources.title: Watermark Central, Cambridge MA: Pedestrian Wind Consultation (RWDI #1601643)
sources.extract: Re-read in r1. Four classes 6/8/10/12 mph GEM at 20% exceedance, 06:00-23:00; safety 56 mph at 0.1%; summer May-Oct, winter Nov-Apr; Boston Logan 1995-2015, anemometer 30 ft; 1200 ft radius, 86 sensors, 36 directions. Walking or strolling suit sidewalks, sitting for terraces and podiums, standing at main entrances.

sources.title: IDCP V3, Cambridge MA: Pedestrian Wind Study (RWDI #2101718)
sources.extract: Generalised flows (downwashing, corner acceleration, channelling); podium set-back, deep canopies, screens; screens at least 6 ft tall and 20-40% porous; guardrails and wrap-around canopies at terrace corners; effect best confirmed by tunnel tests.

sources.title: Wind Study Terms of Reference 2026
sources.extract: Study may be required for buildings of 6 storeys or more; preliminary study with at least 15 sensors; final tunnel study with 1:500 model and 480 m context; comfort judged on wind force, thermal comfort and wind chill.

sources.title: Pedestrian Wind Comfort Assessment Using CFD Simulations With Varying Number of Wind Directions
sources.extract: Re-read in r1 and r2. OpenFOAM steady RANS (realizable k-epsilon) on AIJ case E (Niigata building complex, 60 m high-rise); U_ref at 10 m = 5 m/s, results at 2 m; cylindrical domain height 6 H_max, outlet and lateral 15 H_max, slip top; terrain rough wall z0 = 3.00 m on 0.68 m cells; 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, 4/6/8/10 m/s at 5%, no distress criterion; class agreement by area against 64 directions 79/92/96/99% (4/8/16/32); authors call 8 directions insufficient; Table 5 r 0.61-0.84 (text says 0.71-0.84); mean-speed difference -1% to -35%; no FAC2, hit rate or NMSE.

sources.title: Numerical Study of Flow Structure and Pedestrian Level Wind Comfort Inside Urban Street Canyons (arXiv 1703.08963)
sources.publisher: Pancholy et al., University of Canterbury (preprint)
sources.extract: Idealised steady-RANS canyons; wind comfort via Extended Land Beaufort Scale; gap of 1x height comfortable, 2x height gave a larger uncomfortable zone on the upwind face of the downwind building; building width had little effect.

sources.title: Deriving the operational procedure for the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), Brode et al.
sources.extract: Abstract re-read in r2. UTCI is the air temperature of a reference environment (50% RH with vapour pressure capped at 20 hPa, calm air, radiant temperature equal to air temperature) giving the same dynamic physiological response (UTCI-Fiala model with adaptive clothing); fast polynomial routines and a stress scale are provided. The abstract does not mention the 10 m wind height; full text not opened.

sources.title: ladybug_comfort.parameter.utci documentation
sources.extract: Default UTCI thresholds in deg C: -40, -27, -13, 0, 9 (cold), 26, 28, 32, 38, 46 (heat); Ladybug splits 26-32 into slight and moderate heat stress at 28.

sources.title: ladybug_comfort.utci documentation
sources.extract: Re-read in r1. Wind input is speed 10 m above ground; states 10 m speed is 1.5 times the speed felt at ground in the original Fiala model (no specific citation); UTCI is outdoor only, assumes walking at about 2.4 met; PET recommended otherwise. No validity limits given.

sources.title: pythermalcomfort documentation: models (UTCI)
sources.publisher: Center for the Built Environment, UC Berkeley
sources.extract: Re-read in r1. utci(tdb, tr, v, rh, limit_inputs=True): v is wind at 10 m; limits tdb -50 to 50 C, tr-tdb -30 to 70, v 0.5 to 17 m/s, RH 0-100%, vapour pressure 0-5 kPa; NaN outside limits by default; official program accepts up to 30 m/s but documents 17; approximation can be non-monotonic in wind speed; no pedestrian-to-10 m conversion given.

sources.title: Wind Microclimate Guidelines for Developments in the City of London (August 2019)
sources.extract: Opened in r1, re-read in r2. Approach table by building height (above 100 m: tunnel or CFD for massing, then tunnel and CFD by independent consultants); 36 directions; models within 400 m plus taller buildings beyond; consented or future buildings immediately around the site at any height and those taller than the surrounding average within 300 m, demolished-site case if existing building over 40 m; features over 0.5 m near pedestrians modelled, landscape under 8 m ignored in baselines; Harris-Deaves/ESDU 01008 profile; reference height ideally above 100 m, probabilities scaled to 120 m, scale factors 0.96 (100 m) to 1.48 (600 m); probes at 1.5 m; CFD mesh 0.3 m near critical points, 10 cells across canyon, 3 prism layers below 1.5 m, avoid standard k-epsilon; City Lawson criteria on mean and GEM at 5%: 2.5/4/6/8 m/s with no stated hours window; safety 15 m/s at 0.022%; worst season plus June-August; significance tables; cyclist section (15 m/s applies to cyclists, a probe at least every 40 m on cycling paths); Annex A Weibull fits from Heathrow and City Airport records, not valid for other areas.

sources.title: Glossary, Canadian Climate Data (ECCC)
sources.extract: Re-read in r2. Wind speed usually observed at 10 m as an average over a one-, two- or ten-minute period ending at the observation time; direction a two-minute average in tens of degrees, true (not magnetic), 36 = north, a value of zero denotes calm. r3: the hourly CSV does not use that coding (see S55).

sources.title: Eddy3D docs: Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL)
sources.extract: Re-read in r2. Log-law inflow; reference height Zref default 10 m, reference velocity default 5 m/s per direction, roughness length z0 default 1 m (Revised Davenport terrain classes 0.0002-2 m), ground/displacement height Zgnd; terrain type describes what the wind crosses upwind of the site; one solver case per direction. Silent on wall functions, homogeneity, gradient height and the top boundary.

sources.title: Streamlining meshing methodologies for annual urban CFD simulations (Kastner and Dogan, eSim 2018)
sources.extract: Re-read in r3 (text extracted). AIJ box domain 6 Hmax high, 20 Hmax long (15 Hmax downstream in its figure), blockage at most 3%; cylindrical domain meshed once for 72 or more directions; OpenFOAM 4.1 in Docker 17.12 on Windows 10, one core of a Threadripper 1950X, k-omega SST, SIMPLE with three non-orthogonal correctors, residual targets 1e-4 (p) and 1e-5 (others); lab-scale validation (Jiang et al. 2003, z0 = 0.005 m); coarse 263,919-cell box mesh took 15 h 10 min 47 s; 16 s per iteration (21 s cylindrical) over the first 200 iterations; paper's own extrapolation to 3,000 iterations 13.3 h (box) and 17.5 h (cylindrical); cylindrical domain 21% more cells.

sources.title: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer class description
sources.extract: Opened in r2. U = (u*/kappa) ln((z - zg + z0)/z0) with u* from Uref at Zref; k = u*^2/sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3/(kappa (z - zg + z0)); parameters flowDir, zDir, Uref, Zref, z0, zGround, kappa 0.41, Cmu 0.09. No cap at Zref or at a gradient height.

sources.title: OpenFOAM-12 nutkAtmRoughWallFunction class description
sources.extract: Opened in r2. Provides turbulent kinematic viscosity for atmospheric velocity profiles and is designed to be used with atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity; takes a surface roughness length z0. The description does not state how z0 enters or whether homogeneity is guaranteed.

sources.title: CFD simulation of the atmospheric boundary layer: wall function problems (Blocken, Stathopoulos, Carmeliet)
sources.extract: Not opened (ScienceDirect HTTP 403). The sand-grain relation (about 9.793 z0/Cs) and the horizontal-inhomogeneity problem are recalled from the r2 critique, not read.

sources.title: Technical Documentation, Digital Archive of Canadian Climatological Data (ECCC)
sources.extract: Opened in r2. Hourly wind speed usually observed at 10 m; for aviation stations the average over the two-minute period ending at observation time (one-minute mean until the late 1980s); historical 10-minute means only from synoptic reports four times a day. Direction codes: 36 = north, 00 = calm (archive coding; the hourly CSV leaves direction empty on calms, see S55). Gust speed reported since 1994.

sources.title: OpenFOAM-12 fixedProfileFvPatchField class description
sources.extract: Opened in r3. Fixed-value boundary condition whose value is a Function1 profile (for example a CSV table with outOfBounds clamp) evaluated along a direction from an origin; usable for U, k and epsilon, so a tabulated inlet profile capped above gradient height is possible. codedFixedValue and timeVaryingMappedFixedValue headers are also present in the OpenFOAM-12 tree. No atmospheric example or validation on the page; not run in a case.

Calm = speed 0 with empty direction in every sampled month, never direction 0: 51442 Jan 2025 744 rows (3 timestamp-only), 90 calm of 741 populated; Jul 2020 22; 889 Jan 2000 58; Jul 2010 37; year 2000 542 of 8,780 populated hours; year 2024 272 of 8,766. Empty direction with speed above 0: none. YVR hourly precipitation empty in every sampled month (0 of 8,784 hours in 2024). Station 889 ends 13 Jun 2013 10:00 LST; station 51442 starts 11 Jun 2013 06:00 LST (51 overlap hours: mean difference +0.41 km/h, maximum 4 km/h, 16 hours with direction one 10 degree code apart). Weather text names a sky state in 74% (Jan 2000), 99% (Jul 2010), 31% (Jul 2020), 29% (Jan 2025) of hours.

flags.claim: The City of Vancouver publishes numeric pedestrian wind-comfort criteria or a mandatory wind-study trigger.
flags.detail: None found. vancouver.ca, rezoning.vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, syc.vancouver.ca and council.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 in r1, r2 and again in r3 (curl and WebFetch); the Shape Your City copy of the Higher Buildings Policy is only a download interstitial. Snippets show a qualitative Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion and an example rezoning condition. Ask the Rezoning Centre.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy wording: a higher building should not contribute to adverse microclimate effects.
flags.detail: Taken from search snippets of the 2011 and 2018 versions. The 1997 PDF named in the brief and the current 2026 review documents could not be opened. The 1997 policy as amended governs until Council adopts the updated policy (targeted spring 2027); the amendment trail is unverified.

flags.claim: Default criteria for Vancouver runs are the Toronto 2022 three-class set (Sitting 10, Standing 15, Walking 20 km/h GEM at 80%; safety gust 90 km/h at 0.1% annual).
flags.detail: Chosen as a Canadian downtown tall-building analog because no Vancouver set was found; Hamilton 2026, RWDI mph and City Lawson are selectable, each with its own safety criterion. Edits stay visible as team assumptions. r3: every output carries the AnalogCriteriaLabel until the PrecedentTable holds 2 reports.

flags.claim: Toronto, Hamilton and City of London trigger rules are used as stand-ins for 'when Vancouver requires a wind study'.
flags.detail: All three place a 244-305 m tower in the highest tier (wind-tunnel evidence). Vancouver practice is unconfirmed; for an ideas competition a CFD-level screening is assumed adequate.

flags.claim: Lawson thresholds and RWDI/Toronto thresholds are interchangeable.
flags.correction: They differ in exceedance basis and speed limits: Lawson-type sets use m/s at 5% of time (City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s on mean and GEM); RWDI/Toronto/Hamilton use GEM in km/h or mph at 20%. Using one speed table with the other exceedance gives wrong classes.
flags.detail: M04 enforces one family per run and shows the basis next to each result.

flags.claim: Airport (YVR) or typical-year EPW wind equals the wind at the downtown site.
flags.correction: Toronto requires 30 years of hourly airport data corrected for terrain and scaled via gradient height to the site; a typical-meteorological-year file is not a 30-year record and under-represents storms.
flags.detail: M01 shows a data-quality badge and logs the correction model. r3: the TMYx header reads 'NCEI ISD/ERA5', so the origin of each hour is unverified.

flags.claim: Early CFD can certify gust-safety compliance of a supertall scheme.
flags.correction: Toronto states CFD struggles with separation, eddies and gusts and is not suited to safety-based issues; wind-tunnel testing is required for high triggers. Steady RANS also showed bias against tunnels.
flags.detail: M05 labels outputs by fidelity level and M04 shows safety results as indicative below L3.

flags.claim: Calmer is always better: a Sitting-class wind condition is automatically good for outdoor use.
flags.correction: Toronto notes wind speeds under 5 km/h most of the time can cause low air circulation, exhaust build-up and heat in full sun.
flags.detail: M04 raises a low-wind flag and M06 tests the thermal side. (r2 note: the Toronto note refers to wind speed, not GEM.)

flags.claim: Narrow tower gaps are always windier (simple Venturi rule).
flags.detail: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI describe channelling in narrow gaps, but an idealised steady-RANS study found larger uncomfortable zones at gap = 2x height than at 1x. Non-monotonic and unquantified for supertall towers; M03 distinguishes through-passages from closed gaps.

flags.claim: Infrared.city and other ML surrogates reach 90%+ accuracy within a minute.
flags.detail: Vendor claim; no method or independent validation opened. Training domain unknown; transfer to 244-305 m towers in dense downtown is unproven.

flags.claim: Eddy3D can be embedded in the open-source web tool.
flags.detail: Docs say it is free for all users but state no source licence, and it needs Rhino 8 on Windows or macOS. Treat it as an external tool whose CSV output is imported, until its licence is confirmed. Its GPL-3.0 OpenFOAM solvers are separate.

flags.claim: A hit rate of 66% or more validates a CFD run (COST 732/VDI practice).
flags.detail: Recalled from memory; Toronto only cites COST 732 as the guideline. Original not opened. M05 lists hit rate beside decision-level metrics and does not use it alone.

flags.claim: UTCI wind input equals about 1.5 times the wind felt at ground.
flags.detail: Ladybug documentation attributes the factor to the original Fiala model without citation; pythermalcomfort gives no conversion; the UTCI primary documentation was not opened. Kept as an editable default with a sensitivity band; r2 replaced the fixed 1.5 with a probe-height formula.

flags.claim: Target of at least 50% of occupied hours in the UTCI 'no thermal stress' band; rule weights and cut-offs in the M03 risk index.
flags.detail: No sourced targets. Editable placeholders to be recalibrated against M05 runs and project goals.

flags.claim: Claude Code skills or MCP servers exist for CFD, OpenFOAM or urban wind analysis.
flags.detail: MCP registry and skill catalogue searches returned nothing in r1 and r2 (search budget exhausted in r3, not repeated). A custom MCP wrapper would have to be built.

flags.claim: RWDI and Toronto share one GEM criteria set of 10/15/20 km/h at 80%.
flags.correction: Treat Toronto 2022 (three classes 10/15/20 km/h), Hamilton 2026 (four classes 10/14/17/20 km/h) and RWDI (four classes 6/8/10/12 mph, about 9.7/12.9/16.1/19.3 km/h) as separate CriteriaSets, each with its own safety criterion.
flags.detail: Toronto Table 3 has no Strolling class; RWDI and Hamilton do, and Hamilton's 14 and 17 km/h differ from RWDI's 8 and 10 mph. Evidence: S03, S01, S02, re-read in r1.

flags.claim: Toronto and Hamilton both require at least 16 CFD wind directions.
flags.correction: The 16-direction CFD minimum is Toronto 6.4.2. Hamilton's qualitative CFD may simulate only the prevailing directions (assessment still weights all directions) and Hamilton requires 36 directions only for tunnel tests; City of London asks for 36 in all studies.
flags.detail: Hamilton Technical Requirements 1.A and 1.B (S02), Toronto 6.4.2 (S01), City of London general requirements (S43).

flags.claim: Steady RANS in Hagbo and Giljarhus achieved Pearson r of 0.71-0.84, so 0.71 is the lower end and r can serve as pass/fail.
flags.correction: Table 5 lists r down to 0.61 (247.5 degrees) up to 0.84 (180 degrees); the 0.71-0.84 range comes from the text only. r is scale-invariant and cannot detect the -1% to -35% mean-speed bias the same paper reports, so it is supplementary only.
flags.detail: Frontiers 2022, Table 5 and validation text (S06). M05 uses decision-level metrics (r2).

flags.claim: Butterfly is a viable Python API for an OpenFOAM (Foundation v12) pipeline.
flags.correction: Butterfly is unmaintained: latest commits 11 Sep 2020; the only OpenFOAM compatibility commit seen targets ESI OF1706+. Build case templates directly for the pinned Foundation version or use Eddy3D-generated cases.
flags.detail: GitHub commit history opened in r1 (S16). Foundation v13 also exists (S47), so v12 is pinned deliberately for Eddy3D compatibility.

flags.claim: The Lawson criteria in Hagbo and Giljarhus are a verified mean/GEM criteria set.
flags.correction: The paper uses 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, with no distress or safety criterion. The verified primary Lawson-type set in this packet is the City of London 2019 City Lawson (mean and GEM, 2.5/4/6/8 m/s at 5%, safety 15 m/s at 0.022%).
flags.detail: Hagbo and Giljarhus Table 4 (S06); City of London 2019 (S43). The Hagbo set is kept as comfort-only; safety output is blocked for it.

flags.claim: RWDI considers sidewalks to need strolling or better.
flags.correction: RWDI says conditions comfortable for walking or strolling are appropriate for sidewalks. Sidewalk requirement: Walking, with Strolling as a preference where the set has that class.
flags.detail: RWDI Cambridge report, section 5.1 (S03); Toronto Table 3 also maps sidewalks to Walking (S01).

flags.claim: A modelled context radius of about 350 m is adequate for this tower.
flags.correction: Toronto states 350 m is a minimum and that tall buildings outside it that could influence the site must be included; Hamilton and City of London use 400 m. For H = 244-305 m, 350-400 m is about 1.1-1.6 H and the brief names approved towers of similar height. Use at least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond.
flags.detail: Toronto 6.4.1 (S01), Hamilton 1 (S02), City of London CFD requirements (S43). The 2H term is a team assumption.

flags.claim: Minimum context radius max(400 m, about 2H), with approved and future towers as a mandatory cumulative scenario.
flags.detail: The 350 m and 400 m minima are sourced; the 2H term and the mandatory cumulative case are editable team choices justified by the VTC context. COST 732 and AIJ domain rules were not opened.

flags.claim: Imported VAF data (Eddy3D, tunnel, consultant CSV) share one normalisation reference.
flags.detail: They do not necessarily. The Eddy3D VAF page names no reference height; its ABL component defaults to Zref 10 m, 5 m/s and z0 1 m; City of London uses a reference above 100 m; Hagbo normalise at 10 m. M04 requires a ReferenceSpec on every VAFField and refuses to classify on a mismatch.

flags.claim: ECCC hourly station speeds can be treated as hourly mean winds, and Vancouver Harbour CS provides a usable downtown cross-check.
flags.detail: The averaging part is resolved in r2 (see the r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag). The Harbour CS part is resolved in r3: its hourly files hold no wind after March 1988 (see the r3 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag).

flags.claim: Winter and spring storm winds set the worst comfort class in Vancouver.
flags.detail: The statement came from Ontario practice. Vancouver's strong winds are described as Pacific storms and winter outflow, but no seasonal wind-rose source was opened. M04 derives the governing season from the M01 wind rose instead.

flags.claim: M04 stays core as an importer and classifier; core users get M01-M03 plus M04 only when a VAF file is imported.
flags.detail: Resolves the core-versus-v1 conflict with M05 (hosted OpenFOAM is not feasible before 30 Nov). The UI states that without a VAFField only M03 screening is shown. An Eddy3D workflow guide and import template are the minimal VAF path.

flags.claim: UTCI runs by default on a TMYx time base; calm hours are clipped to 0.5 m/s and hours above 17 m/s are excluded and counted.
flags.detail: TMYx keeps temperature, humidity, solar and wind internally consistent. The 30-year concurrent option has no concurrent solar and is used for cold-stress screening. The clipping rule is a team choice built on the pythermalcomfort limits (S12); excluded hours stay in the denominator.

flags.claim: Weather-protection coverage and wind-driven rain exposure can be judged against Vancouver guidance.
flags.detail: City of Vancouver weather-protection guidance and any rain thresholds could not be opened; ISO 15927-3 not opened. M06 reports relative comparison against the baseline scheme only.

flags.claim: CFD acceptance bands FAC2 at least 0.5, absolute FB at most 0.3, NMSE at most 4.
flags.detail: Recalled from air-quality-model evaluation practice (Chang and Hanna 2004), not opened and not a wind-comfort standard. Withdrawn as acceptance bands in r2.

flags.claim: The Hamilton guideline is an adopted City document.
flags.detail: Text says 'last updated February 20, 2026' but the file name ends 'ph1proposed'; the text also says 'four-season basis' while listing two seasons. Adoption status and season definition should be confirmed with Hamilton staff.

flags.claim: ECCC 1-, 2- or 10-minute mean speeds read higher than hourly means, so unconverted data inflate exceedances; a conversion factor should be applied to reach hourly means.
flags.correction: Treat sampled ECCC means as hourly-mean estimates with no multiplicative conversion. Log the sampling period as metadata, and derive pedestrian gusts from VAF and turbulence only.
flags.detail: A single short-period mean sampled at the observation time has the same expected value as the hourly mean and only more scatter; Durst/ESDU gust-factor curves relate the maximum short-duration mean within an hour to the hourly mean, so they do not apply to one sample. A factor of about 1.05-1.15 would lower every speed; for a Weibull shape near 2, a 10% cut turns a 20% exceedance into about 14%. Evidence: S44, S53 (aviation-station hourly speed is a 2-minute mean ending at the observation), S01, S02, S43. r3: the extra scatter slightly overstates rare high-speed exceedances (conservative; size unquantified).

flags.claim: CFD acceptance bands FAC2 >= 0.5, |FB| <= 0.3, NMSE <= 4 (Chang and Hanna 2004) are suitable placeholders for pedestrian wind-speed validation.
flags.correction: Use decision-level validation: comfort-class agreement and exceedance-probability bias against tunnel data on AIJ benchmark cases, plus the VDI 3783-9 hit rate once opened. Keep FAC2, FB and NMSE descriptive only and adopt no NMSE band.
flags.detail: The bands come from dispersion-model evaluation (concentrations spanning orders of magnitude). For speeds they allow factor-of-2 and 30% bias errors, each enough to shift comfort classes; S06 reports -1% to -35% mean-speed differences that a |FB| <= 0.3 band would partly accept. NMSE recalled differently in r1 and r2; neither source text opened. AIJ case E is a 60 m high-rise complex.

flags.claim: City Lawson comfort is assessed 'for 95% of comfort hours' (the 06:00-23:00 convention).
flags.correction: Run the City Lawson CriteriaSet on 24 h data for comfort and safety, using the Vancouver climate, with only the thresholds transferred, not the London climate coefficients.
flags.detail: The City of London 2019 guideline states no hours restriction in its comfort criteria or results sections; Annex A builds Weibull fits from Heathrow (1973-2017) and City Airport (1988-2017) and says the coefficients are not valid for other areas (S43). The 06:00-23:00 window is Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI practice (S01-S03).

flags.claim: A probe in an empty domain should reproduce the undisturbed profile speed at 1.5 m within 5% when the ABL uses Eddy3D defaults (Zref 10 m, z0 1 m).
flags.correction: Test horizontal homogeneity of U, k and epsilon at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H at the building position. Use an atmospheric rough wall function with the inlet z0 on the approach fetch and a small z0 on the explicitly modelled ground; take the reference speed above 100 m.
flags.detail: With z0 = 1 m, 1.5 m lies in the roughness sublayer and a standard rough wall function needs a sand-grain height near 20 m (about 9.793 z0/Cs, Blocken et al. 2007, recalled, not opened), incompatible with City of London near-ground meshing (0.3 m cells, 3 prism layers below 1.5 m, S43). Eddy3D ABL docs (S46) give defaults Zref 10 m, z0 1 m and are silent on wall functions; OpenFOAM-12 provides nutkAtmRoughWallFunction (S51).

flags.claim: Toronto's low-wind note concerns GEM under 5 km/h.
flags.correction: The note concerns wind speed (mean) under 5 km/h for the majority of the time (e.g. 80%); M04 bases the flag on mean speed and quotes 80% as an example.
flags.detail: Toronto Table 3 note 3 (S01, re-read in r2 and r3).

flags.claim: Station wind is transferred to the site per 22.5 degree sector with a named model, and the default reference height is 120 m.
flags.detail: The downtown site sits on a peninsula, so some sectors cross water (Burrard Inlet, English Bay, False Creek) and others dense city; Eddy3D defines roughness as the terrain the wind crosses upwind (S46). The transfer model is Deaves-Harris/ESDU 01008 as City of London names it, or a log law capped at gradient height (Toronto example 600 m); 120 m is London's convention (S43) applied to Vancouver. Vancouver per-sector z0 values are not sourced; ESDU 01008 was not opened.

flags.claim: Which criteria family, station, seasons and hours City of Vancouver staff accept for downtown tower rezonings.
flags.detail: Attempts in r1-r3 to obtain downtown rezoning wind reports failed (HTTP 403 on all City of Vancouver hosts, including Shape Your City download redirects). The Toronto default stays a team assumption. Action: one named team member downloads two or three reports by hand before 13 Nov and fills the M02 PrecedentTable.

flags.claim: A standard rough wall function with z0 = 1 m needs a sand-grain height ks of about 9.793 z0/Cs, about 20 m.
flags.detail: Relation recalled from Blocken, Stathopoulos and Carmeliet 2007 (S52); the paper could not be opened. Hagbo and Giljarhus ran z0 = 3 m on terrain with 0.68 m cells (S06), so published practice differs. M05 marks the wall-function metric unverified.

flags.claim: Isotropic gust estimates from TKE (sqrt(2k/3)) understate streamwise turbulence by about 20-40%.
flags.detail: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer sets k = u*^2/sqrt(Cmu), about 3.3 u*^2, giving sqrt(2k/3) of about 1.5 u* (S50); surface-layer sigma_u of about 2.4-2.5 u* is recalled, not opened. GEM exceeds the mean only where turbulence intensity exceeds about 28% (1 + 3I > 1.85), so missing turbulence data makes GEM collapse to the mean. M04 declares g and an anisotropy factor and flags RANS-based GEM as indicative.

flags.claim: L2-lite (2-5 M cells, 16 directions, comparative only) and the compute estimates for each fidelity level.
flags.detail: Derived from one reported case (S49) and scaled linearly: 2-5 M cells x 16 directions is roughly 1,800-4,600 core-hours; 20-50 M cells at City of London mesh rules about 18,000-46,000 core-hours (assumption). r3: these are an order of magnitude from one laboratory case, not a lower bound (see the r3 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag); a measured benchmark gate precedes any offer of L2-lite. L2-full is a cluster or consultant task.

flags.claim: Inflow profile capped at gradient height, a consistent top boundary condition, and a declaration up to at least 1.2 H on every VAFField.
flags.detail: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer is an uncapped log law (S50) and the AIJ-style domain for H = 305 m is about 1.8 km high (S49), well above the Toronto 600 m gradient-height example (S01); Hagbo used a slip top (S06). r3: the fixedProfile boundary condition (S54) gives an implementation route (tabulated U, k, epsilon, clamped above gradient height), not yet run in a case; k and epsilon consistent with a capped U are unsourced. The cap, the Richards-Hoxey top condition (recalled) and the 1.2 H declaration are team choices to be validated.

flags.claim: UTCI wind conversion: ln(10/z0)/ln(h/z0) with z0 = 0.01 m, giving 1.47 at 1.1 m and 1.38 at 1.5 m.
flags.detail: The log-law form and z0 = 0.01 m are recalled from the UTCI operational procedure; the PubMed abstract (S08) does not state them and the full text was not opened. The 1.47 value agrees with Ladybug's 1.5 (S11). Applicability of a log law inside a built canopy is unknown.

flags.claim: Passage and podium literature (Blocken et al. on passages; Tsang, Kwok and Hitchcock 2012 on podium, separation and dimensions) supports downgrading the 'narrow gaps accelerate' rule.
flags.detail: Both are recalled from the r2 critique and not opened. The downgrade rests on the opened idealised study (S07), which found a non-monotonic gap effect. M03 separates through-passages from closed gaps and keeps the rule an editable placeholder.

flags.claim: The M03 composite 0-100 risk index stays hidden until a CalibrationLog of at least about 10 massings with L2 runs exists.
flags.detail: No sourced scoring scheme or calibration set exists; a composite number on a board would give false precision to a jury-facing output. The count of 10 is a team placeholder. Per-rule flags are shown instead.

flags.claim: AIJ benchmark cases for a single tall building and a tall building among low-rise blocks are suitable validation targets.
flags.detail: Recalled from the r2 critique; only case E (Niigata complex, 60 m high-rise) was confirmed, via S06. Tominaga et al. 2008 (S40) was not opened; case identities and data access must be checked. No benchmark at 244-305 m was found.

flags.claim: A stability proxy tags Arctic-outflow, clear-night and sea-breeze hours.
flags.detail: Neutral transfer and neutral CFD misrepresent stable and thermally driven hours (Arctic outflow 1-3 times per winter, S37). r3: the ECCC hourly CSV has no cloud column, so the proxy uses a night flag from computed solar elevation, wind class and season, with sky cover only where a source has it (ISD GF1 valid in 18-45% of sampled recent hourly records, EPW total sky cover complete); thresholds are user-editable and unsourced; the tagged share is reported beside the neutral statistics.

flags.claim: Ice and snow shedding from a 244-305 m tower, and wind- and stack-driven drafts at tower entrances and the below-grade transit connection.
flags.detail: No sourced relationship or criterion was found, so no metric is given. M08 emits hand-off notes to P10/SPAC (ice and snow) and SYST (drafts); M04 does not assess them.

flags.claim: ECCC hourly data code calm as direction 0, so 'direction 0 with speed 0' identifies calm hours (M01 'Calm hours handled' was marked verified).
flags.correction: Calm = speed 0 whatever the direction field holds (ECCC hourly CSV: empty; NOAA ISD: type C with direction 999; TMYx: arbitrary direction). Keep calms in the denominator. An empty or 999 direction with speed above 0 is a variable-direction class.
flags.detail: Checked on the files M01 will read (21 Oct 2026). Vancouver Intl A (51442) Jan 2025: 744 rows, 3 timestamp-only, 90 of 741 populated hours have speed 0, all with an empty direction, none with direction 0; Jul 2020 22; Vancouver Int'l A (889) Jan 2000 58 and Jul 2010 37, same pattern; full-year counts 542 of 8,780 (6.2%, year 2000) and 272 of 8,766 (3.1%, year 2024); empty direction with speed above 0 never occurs. The ECCC glossary and technical documentation (S44, S53) describe direction 00 as calm for the archive, but the CSV does not use it. Dropping calms turns a true exceedance E into E/(1 - calm share): 17.6% reads 20.0% at 12.1%, 18.8% at 6.2%, 19.4% at 3.1%, enough to shift a comfort class. Evidence: S55.

flags.claim: Vancouver Harbour CS provides an hourly wind record usable as a downtown cross-check (hourly year options 1976-2026).
flags.correction: No downtown ECCC wind cross-check exists for the last 38 years. Use Harbour CS for temperature, humidity and hourly precipitation only; its 1976-1988 wind record is historical. Refuse the Harbour CS TMYx as a wind file.
flags.detail: Hourly CSV for station 888 (climate ID 1108446): wind present from 20 Jan 1976 to at least 31 Mar 1988, then none in any sampled month (Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, Dec 1988; Jan 1989-1993, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2022, 2024, 2026; Jul 1995 and 2020); the 'year options' in the station search show only that a file exists. VANCOUVER HARBOUR (55438, hourly 2023-2026): sampled Jan and Oct 2024 and Jan and Jul 2025 files hold timestamp rows only. NOAA ISD Harbour CS (712010-99999): WND missing in all 866 records of Jan 2015. Harbour CS TMYx 2011-2025: mean wind 1.0 m/s, 50.3% zero-speed hours, maximum 6.6 m/s, against 3.85 m/s, 3.6% and 19.0 m/s in the YVR TMYx. Evidence: S56, S57, S58, S38.

flags.claim: A 30-year hourly WindClimate can carry one station record id, and series with different ids must never be merged.
flags.correction: Allow a documented StationSplice of YVR climate IDs 1108447 and 1108395 with an overlap check, or use the single-id NOAA ISD record 718920-99999. Apply the no-merge rule between time bases, not inside a documented splice.
flags.detail: ECCC station inventory (modified 30 Sep 2026): VANCOUVER INT'L A 1108447 (station 889) hourly 1953-2013; VANCOUVER INTL A 1108395 (station 51442) hourly 2013-2026. Hourly CSVs: 1108447 ends 13 Jun 2013 10:00 LST, 1108395 starts 11 Jun 2013 06:00 LST; 51 overlapping hours differ by up to 4 km/h (mean +0.41 km/h new minus old) with directions equal in 35 hours and one 10 degree code apart in 16. ISD 718920-99999 is listed as one id from 1955 and agrees with both ECCC sides in June 2013 (mean absolute difference 0.34 and 0.6 km/h). Evidence: S57, S55, S58.

flags.claim: About 57 core-hours per million cells per direction, scaled linearly, is a lower bound for L2-lite cost.
flags.correction: Treat it as an order of magnitude from one laboratory case, label it so on every map, and time one direction of the L2-lite template on the target hardware before offering L2-lite to entrants.
flags.detail: The S49 case is a 263,919-cell laboratory box: OpenFOAM 4.1 in Docker on Windows 10, one core of a 2018 Threadripper 1950X, SIMPLE with three non-orthogonal correctors, residual targets 1e-4 (p) and 1e-5 (others), 16 s per iteration over the first 200 iterations (about 3,400 iterations in 15 h 10 min 47 s), about 61 s per million cells per iteration. Urban atmospheric meshes, tolerances, solver version and hardware differ, so the true figure could be lower or higher by an unquantified factor; 1,800-4,600 core-hours is therefore not a bound.

flags.claim: Toronto and Hamilton give no cyclist rule.
flags.correction: Hamilton names cyclist areas and bicycle lanes as test locations under its standard pedestrian criteria; Toronto's guide has no cyclist text; only City of London adds a cyclist-specific safety note (15 m/s, a probe at least every 40 m).
flags.detail: Hamilton 2026 (S02): the scope defines cyclist areas (frontages, pathways, entrances, open spaces, bicycle parking, bicycle routes), test locations include bicycle lanes adjacent to the building, and the Walking class text mentions cycling; no separate threshold. Toronto ToR (S01): a text search finds no cyclist or bicycle wording. City of London (S43) unchanged.

flags.claim: A downtown anemometer record of 10 or more years (Metro Vancouver air-quality network, port or rooftop stations) exists to calibrate the airport-to-downtown transfer.
flags.detail: Named only as an unverified candidate; no station, record length or licence was opened (one Metro Vancouver page lookup returned Page Not Found). Until one is verified, M01 reports that no downtown cross-check exists and relies on the per-sector transfer.

flags.claim: Every comfort or safety output carries a fixed AnalogCriteriaLabel until the PrecedentTable holds at least 2 downtown Vancouver reports.
flags.detail: Prevents Toronto, Hamilton, RWDI or City Lawson classes being shown as Vancouver compliance. Label wording: 'Criteria: [family, version] analog (team assumption). No City of Vancouver numeric criteria found. Precedent reports: n'. The 2-report threshold is a team choice; the export validator for PRES boards belongs to the presentation packet and M02 supplies the string.

flags.claim: All series are stored in UTC with an LST field and the comfort window 06:00-23:00 is read as Local Standard Time by default.
flags.detail: ECCC stamps LST (UTC-8), ISD UTC (08:00Z matches ECCC 00:00 LST), the TMYx header gives -8.0 and daylight saving No; Toronto and Hamilton state the window with no time zone. The LST default is a team choice, editable and logged in the CriteriaSet. The EPW dictionary page (S59) does not say standard or daylight time; the header and a June solar-peak check support standard time for the TMYx files.

flags.claim: TMYx wind, direction and precipitation fields are station observations.
flags.detail: Headers read 'NCEI ISD/ERA5'. The YVR TMYx has 334 distinct direction values (ISD directions come in 10 degree codes), 313 zero-speed hours with non-zero directions, and a precipitation field summing to 1,795 mm against 957.6 mm measured at YVR in 2025 (ECCC daily; one year, not a normal). Per-hour source flags were not decoded, so the origin and bias of TMYx wind and rain are unverified; M01 and M06 label them so.

unresolved_relationships: Quantified reduction of pedestrian-level GEM per metre of tower-to-podium step-back, podium height or canopy depth (direction sourced, magnitude not); Tsang, Kwok and Hitchcock 2012 on podium, separation and tall-building dimensions is recalled and not opened.

Gap-to-height ratio that minimises channelling between adjacent supertall towers (Venturi versus buffeting); only idealised low-rise RANS results seen (S07); passage studies reporting wind-blocking not opened.

Dominant strong-wind directions and speeds at the downtown Vancouver site compared with Vancouver International Airport, including Burrard Inlet channelling and winter outflow; no downtown anemometer record is verified (Harbour CS wind ended in 1988), so site data or a consultant study would be needed.
Percentage speed reduction from chamfered, rounded, stepped or re-entrant corners on a 244-305 m tower.

General effectiveness of wind screens, canopies and trees beyond the single RWDI project (screens at least 1.8 m tall, 20-40% porous), including winter versus summer foliage; no sourced leaf area density values for porous-media tree runs ('City in Nature' planting, link to ECOL).

How Vancouver staff and the Urban Design Panel judge 'adverse microclimate effects' under the Higher Buildings Policy (no numeric rule found); downtown rezoning wind reports were not obtainable in r1-r3 (HTTP 403), so the accepted criteria family, station, seasons and hours are unknown.

Correct conversion between pedestrian-level (1.5 m) speed and the 10 m wind input of UTCI: the log-law factor (1.38 at 1.5 m, 1.47 at 1.1 m) rests on z0 = 0.01 m and 1.1 m recalled from the UTCI procedure; primary text not opened; validity inside a built canopy unknown.
Effect of neighbouring approved or future towers (named in the brief) on wind at the site, and how a Vancouver review would define the cumulative scenario.
Accuracy of ML surrogates and steady RANS for 244-305 m towers, and for terraces at height; no validation found; AIJ case E has only a 60 m high-rise.
Effect of corner treatment, taper and tower height on structural wind loads and vortex shedding; deferred to P10 (confirm the current Vancouver Building By-law edition first).

Size of the extra sampling scatter that single 1- or 2-minute ECCC means add to exceedance statistics (direction: slight overstatement of rare high-speed exceedances, reasoned; size not quantified), and whether 10 degree direction codes, integer km/h resolution and the proportional allocation to 22.5 degree sectors bias sector exceedances.

Vancouver-specific per-sector roughness, displacement height and gradient height, and internal-boundary-layer development for water-to-city transitions (Burrard Inlet, English Bay, False Creek); ESDU 01008 was not opened and applicability to Vancouver is unverified.
Effect of atmospheric stability (Arctic outflow, clear nocturnal hours, sea breeze) on the exposure transfer and on neutral-inflow CFD; no sourced proxy thresholds.
Validity of a log-law or Deaves-Harris inflow profile and of the top boundary condition for 244-305 m towers in a domain about 1.8 km high; terraces at 150-300 m.

Turbulent kinetic energy and dissipation profiles consistent with a tabulated U profile capped above gradient height (fixedProfile route, S54), and the matching top boundary condition: no sourced formulation; to be tested in the empty-domain homogeneity run.
Normalisation convention of Eddy3D VAF output (the VAF page names no reference; the ABL component defaults to 10 m, 5 m/s, z0 1 m).

Decision-level acceptance bands for CFD validation (class agreement, exceedance bias) and the COST 732/VDI 3783-9 hit rate: primary texts not opened; identity and data access of the AIJ single-tall-building and tall-building-among-low-rise cases unconfirmed.

Whether the AIJ and COST 732 domain rules read second-hand (6 Hmax high, 20 Hmax long, blockage at most 3%) suffice for 305 m towers in dense context, and how blockage is computed with explicit neighbouring towers.

Measured wall time, iterations, cell counts and residual targets for one direction of the L2-lite template on the target hardware; the only data point is a 0.26 M cell laboratory case in Docker on Windows (S49).

Which ground-roughness set-up gives better pedestrian-level agreement: a large z0 on the whole ground as in Hagbo (z0 = 3 m, 0.68 m cells) or an atmospheric rough wall upstream with a small z0 on modelled ground; untested here, and the sand-grain relation (Blocken 2007) is recalled.
Anisotropy factor for gusts derived from RANS TKE (surface-layer sigma_u of about 2.4-2.5 u* is recalled) and its validity in wakes.
Cyclist-specific wind criteria beyond City of London's 15 m/s limit (Hamilton applies its pedestrian criteria to bicycle lanes; Toronto is silent) and the cycle-route layout implied by the brief.
Ice and snow shedding from a 244-305 m tower onto the public realm and transit plaza: no sourced relationship; hand-off to P10 and SPAC.
Wind- and stack-driven drafts at tower entrances and the below-grade secondary transit connection: no sourced criteria; hand-off to SYST.

Wind-driven rain exposure versus canopy depth, whether a two-station composite (Harbour CS precipitation with YVR wind, 13.0 km apart) represents rain at the site, and the Vancouver weather-protection requirements; driving-rain method ISO 15927-3 not opened.

Whether any downtown anemometer record of 10 or more years exists (Metro Vancouver air-quality network, port or rooftop stations are unverified candidates) to calibrate the airport-to-downtown transfer.

Whether the ECCC splice (11-13 Jun 2013 overlap, 51 h) and the ISD record stay equivalent over the full 30 years: anemometer height, exposure and instrument changes are not documented in the sources opened.

A complete sky-cover source for the 30-year base after 2013: ISD GF1 total coverage is valid in 18-45% of sampled recent hourly records and the ECCC Weather text names a sky state in 29-31% of recent sampled hours; EPW total sky cover is complete but of unverified origin.

Origin and bias of TMYx wind, direction and precipitation (header 'NCEI ISD/ERA5'): the YVR TMYx precipitation field sums to 1,795 mm against 957.6 mm measured at YVR in 2025; per-hour source flags not decoded.
Concurrent hourly solar for a 30-year record: no co-located series identified; TMYx radiation is a typical year.
Effect of climate change on Vancouver wind and temperature statistics; OneBuilding lists NRC future-climate EPW locations for Canada (not opened), so the stationary-climate limit may be relaxable.
Governing season for Vancouver pedestrian wind: derive from the M01 wind rose rather than assume.
Number of L2-calibrated massings needed before the M03 composite risk index is meaningful (about 10 is a team placeholder).
How Vancouver reviewers read the 06:00-23:00 comfort window with respect to time zone and daylight saving (Toronto and Hamilton state no zone); LST is a team default.
change_log: Round 1: Built P03 with 8 modules: wind climate (M01), trigger and criteria selector (M02), massing screening (M03), comfort and safety classifier (M04), CFD and surrogate engine (M05), UTCI (M06), mitigation advisor (M07), elevated terraces (M08).

Round 1: Replaced the assumption 'Vancouver has its own wind criteria' with analog Canadian municipal criteria after no Vancouver numeric criteria could be found or opened; flagged UNVERIFIED and TEAM_ASSUMPTION.
Round 1: Corrected FALSE ASSUMPTIONS: Lawson and RWDI limits are not interchangeable; airport or typical-year wind is not site wind; early CFD cannot certify gust safety; calm is not always better.
